column2: Inquiry
column3: Forespoergsel

column2:
Your esteemed {%V:0E} {%N:0F},

You have been recommended to me as a quick and reliable maritime trader. I have a small problem and I would like to graciously request your service.

A few courier duties have to be carried out quickly and the captain who had agreed and gave me his word of honour, did not, unfortunately, keep his word and has not appeared.

A number of packages and documents of the highest importance have to be delivered to various towns. The quicker you are, the more I will reward you.

Please decide within ten days.

P.S.
Your journey begins in {%t:04}.

{%V:06} {%N:07} of {%t:04}
column3:
Hoejtaerede {%V:0E} {%N:0F},

I er blevet anbefalet mig som en hurtig og paalidelig soehandelsmand. Jeg har et lille problem og vil ydmygst bede om jeres tjeneste.

Nogle kureraerinder skal udfoeres i hast, og kaptajnen, der havde lovet det og givet mig sit aeresord, har desvaerre ikke holdt det og er ikke moedt op.

En raekke pakker og dokumenter af stoerste vigtighed skal bringes til forskellige byer. Jo hurtigere I er, desto bedre vil jeg beloenne jer.

Beslut jer venligst inden ti dage.

P.S.
Jeres rejse begynder i {%t:04}.

{%V:06} {%N:07}
column3:
O glaede!

Jeg vidste, I var til at stole paa.

Moed op i {%t:04} senest den {%D:05}. Der skal vaere mindst 3 \L ledigt paa jeres skib.

{%V:06} {%N:07}

column2: Let's begin
column3: Lad os begynde

column2:
Well now, the cargo is on board and sails await favourable wind.

But first, my presence is required in {%t:0D}. Take me there as quickly as the tides of fate allow.

After my arrival in {%t:0D} I will meet a trader. Stay at anchor in the harbour in the meantime so that I can give you the next destination.

Do not forget: the quicker I travel, the higher my payment - and your share.

{%V:06} {%N:07}
column3:
Nuvel, lasten er om bord, og sejlene venter paa gunstig vind.

Men foerst kraeves min tilstedevaerelse i {%t:0D}. Bring mig derhen, saa hurtigt skaebnens tidevand tillader det.

Efter min ankomst til {%t:0D} skal jeg moedes med en handelsmand. Bliv imens liggende for anker i havnen, saa jeg kan give jer det naeste maal.

Glem ikke: jo hurtigere jeg rejser, desto hoejere bliver min betaling - og jeres andel.

{%V:06} {%N:07}

column2: Our journey
column3: Vores rejse

column2: Along please...
column3: Videre, tak...

column2: Too slow!
column3: For langsomt!

column2:
What stigma on your reputation!

I must say that I have never travelled in so slowly.

We sailed for {%B:0B} days.

I would rather take an oxen cart across the country the next time, or better still, use the power of my own arms and swim rather than travel with you again!

Now to your payment: It is worth as much as your word and your reputation! Absolutely nothing. Did I not most clearly tell you at the beginning of our journey, that I was in a hurry?

Be that as it may. Farewell and I never want to see you again!

{%V:06} {%N:07}
column3:
Sikken en plet paa jeres ry!

Jeg maa sige, at jeg aldrig har rejst saa langsomt.

Vi sejlede i {%B:0B} dage.

Naeste gang tager jeg hellere en oksekaerre over land, eller endnu bedre svoemmer for egen kraft, end at rejse med jer igen!

Nu til jeres betaling: den er lige saa meget vaerd som jeres ord og jeres ry! Absolut ingenting. Sagde jeg ikke tydeligt ved rejsens begyndelse, at jeg havde travlt?

Lige meget. Farvel, og jeg vil aldrig se jer igen!

{%V:06} {%N:07}

column2: Reward
column3: Beloenning

column2:
My courier journey ends here.

I will leave the ship today and take the rest of my packages with me.
After that, I will no longer require your services as I intend, in the spirit of friendship, to visit an old acquaintance.

My profound thanks for the speedy transport.

I am sure you will be well satisfied with the amount of  {%B:0C}\C for your efforts.

Respectfully, bow I before thee with the deepest respect.

{%V:06} {%N:07}
column3:
Min kurerrejse slutter her.

Jeg forlader skibet i dag og tager resten af mine pakker med.
Derefter har jeg ikke laengere brug for jeres tjenester, for jeg agter i venskab at besoege en gammel bekendt.

Min dybe tak for den hurtige transport.

Jeg er sikker paa, at summen af {%B:0C}\C vil tilfredsstille jer vel for jeres umage.

Med den dybeste aerboedighed bukker jeg for jer.

{%V:06} {%N:07}

column2: Secret
column3: Hemmelighed

column2:
Greetings to you {%V:0E} {%N:0F},

Now that the light of my eyes is getting shadowy and the long sleep is getting closer, I'll tell you a secret. Many years ago, when I was in the service of the Hanse and while I was chasing a pirate; the ship of an influential long distance merchant sank. I later heard that it was carrying a valuable cargo. Gold and jewellery are supposedly resting in this wet grave. Unfortunately, I never had the chance to recover this treasure. Against a contribution of  {%B:06}\C to sweeten my old days, I'll give you a part of the treasure map.

Art thou interested?

Humblest
{%V:0C} {%N:0D}
column3:
Hil jer, {%V:0E} {%N:0F},

Nu da lyset i mine oejne formoerkes, og den lange soevn naermer sig, vil jeg fortaelle jer en hemmelighed. For mange aar siden, da jeg tjente Hansaen og jagede en pirat, sank skibet tilhoerende en indflydelsesrig fjernhandelsmand. Senere hoerte jeg, at det foerte en kostbar last. Guld og juveler skulle hvile i denne vaade grav. Desvaerre fik jeg aldrig lejlighed til at bjaerge skatten. Mod et bidrag paa {%B:06}\C til at forsoede mine gamle dage giver jeg jer en del af skattekortet.

Er I interesseret?

Ydmygst
{%V:0C} {%N:0D}

column2:
Ahoy, Scoundrel!

Listen, you are {%6:00}for a small adventure. {%t:03} years ago I hired on the {%Q:07}. Our captain has not said a lot about the cargo. But at nights in our cabins we have heard whisperings about treasures... But the ship was rotten and didn't stand up to the long hard journey. It sank, and with it, a lot of seamen and the captain. Sir, I do not have the means myself to search for the treasure. But I'm prepared to sell you my part of the map for the sum of {%B:06}\C.

Interested?

{%V:0C} {%N:0D}
column3:
Ohoej, slyngel!

Hoer her, er du {%6:00}frisk paa et lille eventyr? For {%t:03} aar siden moenstrede jeg paa {%Q:07}. Vores kaptajn sagde ikke meget om lasten. Men om natten i koejerne hoerte vi hvisken om skatte... Men skibet var raaddent og holdt ikke til den lange, haarde rejse. Det sank, og med det mange soemaend og kaptajnen. Herre, selv har jeg ikke midler til at lede efter skatten. Men jeg vil gerne saelge jer min del af kortet for {%B:06}\C.

Interesseret?

column2: Sought pirate
column3: Eftersoegt pirat

column2:
Greetings to you, {%V:06} {%N:0F},

Would you be interested in doing me a great service, for which I would richly reward you?  It has something to do with a evil pirate to whom I once lost my proudest ship. After many months of searching I have finally succeeded in catching up with him. I smuggled a spy into his place; who recently reported to me. So that I now know of the pirate's secret place of residence.
Will you visit his hideaway and once and for all rid the world of him? This deed would be worth {%B:08}\C to me.

{%V:0A} {%N:0C}
column3:
Hil jer, {%V:06} {%N:0F},

Vil I goere mig en stor tjeneste, som jeg vil beloenne rigeligt? Det drejer sig om en ond pirat, som jeg engang mistede mit stolteste skib til. Efter mange maaneders soegen er det endelig lykkedes mig at indhente ham. Jeg har smuglet en spion ind hos ham, som for nylig aflagde rapport. Saa nu kender jeg piratens hemmelige opholdssted.
Vil I opsoege hans skjulested og én gang for alle befri verden for ham? Den daad ville vaere {%B:08}\C vaerd for mig.

{%V:0A} {%N:0C}

column2: Pirate killed

column2:

Therefore, you do not deserve the promised pay.

May luck be with you in your future endeavors.

column3:

Derfor fortjener I ikke den lovede loen.

Maa lykken foelge jer i jeres fremtidige foretagender.

column2:

He has escaped because you were too slow!

Of course I withdraw my generous reward. This was the last mission I entrusted you with!

column3:
Det meldes, at piraten har faaet nys om vores plan og er flyttet til et andet skjulested!

Han er sluppet vaek, fordi I var for langsom!

Naturligvis traekker jeg min gavmilde beloenning tilbage. Det var den sidste opgave, jeg betroede jer!

{%V:0A} {%N:0C}

column2: Mission goal
column3: Opgavens maal

column2:
You have got one year to advance from a small shopkeeper to a trader.

Lubeck's strength is fishing and the production of iron goods. Apart from that, wood and tiles are also produced so it should not be a problem to build new buildings. 

You should therefore concentrate in getting beer from Stetin or Gdansk in the first instance. You could also go to Hamburg or Bremen, but these are further away. 

There is sometimes a lack of iron goods and fish in Danzig. Stetin also urgently needs iron goods. 

Make sure that you do not pay too much for these goods. The limits are somewhere between 450 for fish, 450 for iron goods and 50 for beer.
column3:
I har ét aar til at avancere fra kraemmer til handelsmand.

Luebecks styrke er fiskeriet og fremstillingen af jernvarer. Desuden fremstilles trae og tagsten, saa det burde ikke vaere noget problem at opfoere nye bygninger.

Koncentrer jer derfor foerst om at skaffe oel fra Stettin eller Gdansk. I kan ogsaa sejle til Hamburg eller Bremen, men de ligger laengere vaek.

I Gdansk mangler der af og til jernvarer og fisk. Ogsaa Stettin har haardt brug for jernvarer.

Soerg for ikke at betale for meget for disse varer. Graenserne ligger omkring 450 for fisk, 450 for jernvarer og 50 for oel.

column2: Mission hint
column3: Raad til opgaven

column2:
Because the trade with pig iron is important, you should make sure that there is always enough pig iron available in Lubeck; then this raw material cannot be produced here. But it can, for example, be produced in Oslo. This town is also a grateful importer of grain, iron goods and beer.

You should sell as much of these goods as possible in Lubeck, then that is the quickest way of raising your status, and your advancement to trader will then be quicker. 

Incidentally, in this part of the campaign you should build neither ships nor buildings. We will do that in the next part.
column3:
Da handlen med raajern er vigtig, boer I soerge for, at der altid er nok raajern i Luebeck, for dette raastof kan ikke fremstilles der. Det fremstilles for eksempel i Oslo. Den by aftager ogsaa gerne korn, jernvarer og oel.

Saelg saa meget som muligt af disse varer i Luebeck; det er den hurtigste maade at oege jeres anseelse paa, og saa bliver I hurtigere handelsmand.

I denne del af kampagnen skal I i oevrigt hverken bygge skibe eller bygninger. Det goer vi i naeste del.

column2:
You are on the right way! 
But in order to become a trader, you'll have to start looking after the rich citizens of Lubeck as well. They are not really interested in grain and beer; you should try to satisfy their demand by supplying them with meat, wine and cloth. 

You'll get meat from Aalborg and Bergen. Make sure that Aalborg gets enough salt, otherwise they cannot produce any meat there. You can take the salt with you from Lubeck.

You'll get wine from Cologne; the citizens there could well do with some fish and beer. 

You can get cloth from Bisbee. Find out what they need there.
column3:
I er paa rette vej!
Men for at blive handelsmand maa I ogsaa tage jer af Luebecks rige borgere. Korn og oel interesserer dem ikke rigtig; proev at daekke deres efterspoergsel efter koed, vin og klaede.

Koed faar I i Aalborg og Bergen. Soerg for, at Aalborg har salt nok, ellers kan man ikke fremstille koed der. Saltet kan I tage med fra Luebeck.

Vin faar I i Cologne; borgerne der kunne godt bruge lidt fisk og oel.

Klaede finder I i Visby. Find ud af, hvad man har brug for der.

column2:
Normally, your reputation in a town will always then grow, when you supply it with goods. However, this is only valid if the goods are also needed. When a product is no longer needed, there will not be much between the purchasing and selling prices You should keep an eye on this.

Incidentally, you can also lose your standing in a town if you buy up a rare product. So never do that in your hometown!
column3:
Normalt vokser jeres anseelse i en by, naar I forsyner den med varer. Det gaelder dog kun, hvis varerne ogsaa er efterspurgte. Naar en vare ikke laengere efterspoerges, bliver der kun lille forskel paa indkoebs- og salgspris. Hold oeje med det.

I kan i oevrigt ogsaa miste anseelse i en by, hvis I opkoeber en sjaelden vare. Goer det derfor aldrig i jeres hjemby!

column2: You will have noticed some small product symbols in various towns on the sea chart. These show you which products are most needed. \nAttention: It could take some time before this information reaches you; it is therefore possible that a symbol becomes invalid, before you reach the town.  If you want to use these symbols to your advantage and make additional profit, then concentrate on the towns in the immediate area in and around Lubeck.
column3: I har sikkert bemaerket smaa varesymboler ved forskellige byer paa soekortet. De viser, hvilke varer der er mest brug for.\nBemaerk: det kan tage tid, foer nyhederne naar jer, saa et symbol kan vaere foraeldet, inden I naar byen. Vil I udnytte symbolerne til ekstra fortjeneste, saa koncentrer jer om byerne i Luebecks naerhed.

column2: Winter is coming! Buy grain and beer and store it in your trading office so that you are in a position to supply your hometown in winter and thereby increase your standing among its citizens. \n
column3: Vinteren naermer sig! Koeb korn og oel og oplagr det i jeres kontor, saa I kan forsyne jeres hjemby om vinteren og derved oege jeres anseelse blandt borgerne.\n

column2: Remember that your rank is awarded by your hometown; you must therefore do everything in your power to become well known in the town. Your current rank is displayed in the overview of your trading office.\nYou have to do more for the citizens of your hometown in order to advance.\n
column3: Husk, at jeres rang tildeles af jeres hjemby; goer derfor alt, hvad der staar i jeres magt, for at blive kendt i byen. Jeres nuvaerende rang vises i oversigten over jeres kontor.\nI maa goere mere for borgerne i jeres hjemby for at avancere.\n

column2:
In this part of the campaign you must advance from a trader to a merchant. You have six months to do so. Alongside trading, you should now build facilities and houses in your hometown.

As you know, Lubeck is strong in fishing and the production of iron goods. Now build a building of each production. You might eventually have to get the building raw materials from other towns. However, just build one of each type of building for the moment; then you need to find customers for your products.

Building production facilities give you two advantages apart from trading: Firstly, your standing increases with every worker you employ. Secondly, the jobs you are offering attract new citizens to the town. This increases the demand and you can sell more goods.

In order for your production facility to quickly reach full capacity, the poor citizens must at least be satisfied. You should continue to ensure a good supply of goods to the town. Apart from that, the workers need living quarters. If the capacity of the previous houses is not enough to accommodate the workers, then you should build a new house.
column3:
I denne del af kampagnen skal I avancere fra handelsmand til koebmand. I har seks maaneder til det. Ved siden af handlen boer I nu bygge vaerksteder og huse i jeres hjemby.

Som I ved, er Luebeck staerk i fiskeri og fremstilling af jernvarer. Byg nu en bygning til hver af disse produktioner. Maaske maa I hente byggematerialerne fra andre byer. Byg dog foreloebig kun én bygning af hver slags; derefter maa I finde koebere til jeres varer.

Vaerksteder giver jer to fordele ud over handlen: for det foerste stiger jeres anseelse med hver arbejder, I ansaetter. For det andet traekker de arbejdspladser, I tilbyder, nye borgere til byen. Det oeger efterspoergslen, og I kan saelge flere varer.

For at jeres vaerksted hurtigt kan naa fuld kapacitet, skal de fattige i det mindste vaere tilfredse. Bliv derfor ved med at forsyne byen godt. Desuden har arbejderne brug for boliger. Raekker de eksisterende huse ikke til arbejderne, boer I bygge et nyt hus.

column2:
Remember that your production facilities need raw materials. This should be available in your trading office. 

If you have a trading office administrator, then he can buy the raw materials from the town, if necessary. That however, is not necessary at the moment, and in any case an administrator only cost money.

To find out what raw materials you need in your production facilities; you have to click them when they are completed. You can also get information on the requirement of your facilities in the town in your trading office.
column3:
Husk, at jeres vaerksteder skal bruge raavarer. De boer findes i jeres kontor.

Har I en kontorforvalter, kan han om noedvendigt koebe raavarerne i byen. Det er dog ikke noedvendigt lige nu, og en forvalter koster kun penge.

For at se, hvilke raavarer jeres vaerksteder skal bruge, klikker I paa dem, naar de er faerdige. I jeres kontor finder I ogsaa oplysninger om jeres vaerksteders behov i byen.

column2:
Essentially, in order to become a merchant, you must gain social recognition and build up considerable wealth. Again, concentrate on wine, meat and cloth. Now add skins to your assortment, you will find these in the East.  

Should you by chance come across spices, then take these with you and sell them also in Lubeck; then the rich are very hot on them.
column3:
For at blive koebmand maa I frem for alt vinde socialt anseelse og opbygge en betydelig formue. Koncentrer jer igen om vin, koed og klaede. Foej nu skind til jeres sortiment; dem finder I mod oest.

Skulle I tilfaeldigvis stoede paa krydderier, saa tag dem med og saelg dem ogsaa i Luebeck; de rige er vilde med dem.

column2:
In order to be able to transport the goods that you produce better, you should own one more ship at least. Place an order at the ship builders in Lubeck for a snaikka or a crayer. 

Use the shipyard in Lubeck as much as possible, including repair work, because the more orders they get the better the ships they build will be.
column3:
For bedre at kunne fragte de varer, I fremstiller, boer I eje mindst ét skib mere. Bestil en snekke eller en kraier hos skibsvaerftet i Luebeck.

Giv vaerftet i Luebeck saa meget arbejde som muligt, reparationer medregnet, for jo flere ordrer det faar, desto bedre bliver de skibe, det bygger.

column2: You are on the right way; your social standing is growing all the time.
column3: I er paa rette vej; jeres anseelse vokser hele tiden.

column2:
Your social standing in Lubeck is sufficient now; try to keep it at this level. 

But you cannot afford to neglect the poorer citizens of the town. If you do not look after a particular group of citizens for a while, then your status will fall again. 

Supply the rich in Lubeck as before, but strengthen your efforts to cover the supply requirement of the poor.
column3:
Jeres anseelse i Luebeck er nu tilstraekkelig; proev at holde den paa dette niveau.

Men I har ikke raad til at forsoemme byens fattigere borgere. Forsoemmer I en gruppe borgere i et stykke tid, falder jeres anseelse igen.

Forsyn de rige i Luebeck som hidtil, men oeg jeres anstrengelser for at daekke de fattiges behov.

column2:
You have achieved enough recognition in Lubeck. 

Unfortunately, you are not wealthy enough to advance to the rank of a merchant. Continue to look after the citizens of Lubeck, and try at the same time to build up greater wealth. 

Good luck.
column3:
I har opnaaet nok anseelse i Luebeck.

Desvaerre er I ikke formuende nok til at avancere til koebmands rang. Bliv ved med at tage jer af Luebecks borgere, og proev samtidig at opbygge en stoerre formue.

Held og lykke.

column2: You only need a bit more social recognition and a bit more wealth to advance from merchant to travelling merchant. Besides that, you have to become a member of the guild; the latter gives you a few more reputation points anyway.
column3: I mangler kun lidt mere anseelse og lidt mere formue for at avancere fra koebmand til rejsende koebmand. Desuden skal I blive medlem af lavet; det giver jer alligevel nogle point anseelse.

column2:
Remember, that it is not only cash, which counts as wealth but also production facilities, houses, ships and goods in stock. Monies that you owe to a lender are deducted.

In case accommodation in Lubeck is becoming short, then you should quickly build the relevant houses, then every tenant- in exactly the same way as every worker you employ- will gets you additional points. If you are not quick enough, then a competitor or the town could build the houses and that would then make it more difficult for you fill your own. Because there is also a weekly property tax on the houses, you have to have a high rate of occupancy in order to make a profit. Half-timbered houses must have an occupancy rate of over 70{%%:00} other houses of over 50{%%:00}.
column3:
Husk, at ikke kun rede penge regnes som formue, men ogsaa vaerksteder, huse, skibe og varer paa lager. Penge, I skylder en laangiver, traekkes fra.

Begynder der at blive mangel paa boliger i Luebeck, boer I hurtigt bygge de noedvendige huse, for hver lejer giver jer - ligesom hver arbejder, I ansaetter - ekstra point. Er I ikke hurtige nok, kan en konkurrent eller byen bygge husene, og saa bliver det svaerere at fylde jeres egne. Da husene ogsaa paalaegges en ugentlig grundskat, skal I have hoej belaegning for at tjene penge. Bindingsvaerkshuse skal have en belaegning paa over 70{%%:00}, andre huse paa over 50{%%:00}.

column2: Have you joined the guild in Lubeck yet? You have to become a member of the guild to advance to a long distance merchant or even higher. Incidentally, the wealthier you are the higher the fee for joining. Besides, it decreases in proportion to your social standing, the higher your status the less you pay.\n
column3: Er I allerede traadt ind i lavet i Luebeck? I skal vaere medlem af lavet for at avancere til fjernhandelsmand eller endnu hoejere. I oevrigt: jo rigere I er, desto hoejere indskud. Det falder dog med jeres anseelse: jo hoejere anseelse, desto mindre betaler I.\n

column2:
You will have to achieve a decisively higher status among all citizens of the town within a year. Because you have to be considerably wealthier, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown, then investing your money increases your wealth and brings recognition.
Double or triple your production in Lubeck and build houses in time, so that the workers and their families can become your tenants. 
Increasing the production also means that you will have to build new ships, to enable you to transport your products.
column3:
I maa inden for et aar opnaa en klart hoejere anseelse blandt alle byens borgere. Da I skal vaere betydeligt rigere, boer I investere saa meget som muligt i jeres hjemby, for investeringer oeger formuen og giver anseelse.
Fordobl eller tredobl jeres produktion i Luebeck, og byg huse i tide, saa arbejderne og deres familier kan blive jeres lejere.
Oeget produktion betyder ogsaa, at I maa bygge nye skibe for at kunne fragte jeres varer.

column2:
Here are few more tips on how to achieve respectability. Basically, you should bear in mind that  everything you do for your hometown; will bring you status points. Donate your money to the church or to the bathhouse; this will increase it. Lend it, or build a building and facilities; this also increases it.  It will also increase through: the family, organising festivities, great wealth or placing outriggers at the disposal of the town. 
Your respectability can sink in the same way if, for example, a crime becomes known, if your production facility is demolished or if you demand too high an interest when lending money.
Incidentally, your status can increase by a successful expedition, then all Hanse towns profit from such undertakings. You can undertake such expeditions from time to time and discover new trans-shipment locations.
column3:
Her er nogle flere raad om, hvordan I vinder agtelse. Husk frem for alt, at alt, hvad I goer for jeres hjemby, giver jer anseelse. Skaenk penge til kirken eller badstuen; det oeger den. Laan penge ud eller byg bygninger og vaerksteder; det oeger den ogsaa. Den stiger desuden gennem familien, ved at holde fester, ved stor formue eller ved at stille forsvarsskibe til byens raadighed.
Jeres agtelse kan synke paa samme maade, hvis for eksempel en forbrydelse bliver kendt, hvis jeres vaerksted rives ned, eller hvis I kraever for hoej rente, naar I laaner penge ud.
En vellykket ekspedition kan i oevrigt ogsaa oege jeres anseelse, for alle hansestaeder nyder godt af saadanne foretagender. Fra tid til anden kan I foretage saadanne ekspeditioner og opdage nye omladningssteder.

column2:
So that you can make even more profit, you should build trading offices in as many other towns as possible and produce goods in them. Your own production is not always cheaper than goods, which you can sometimes buy at favourable prices. However, your own production at a constant price and constant quantity makes calculation easier. This is ideal, for example, for setting up trades routes to continuously supply your hometown or to exchange your own products between two or more trading offices.
But be careful in your choice of production facilities. Think carefully about the goods that will be needed in towns in the future. Then if you produce more than you can sell, then surplus goods will have to be held in stock. and as a result of that, your profit will drop permanently.  
If you cannot make a profit from your own production, then do not be afraid of closing or demolishing such a facility.
column3:
For at tjene endnu mere boer I bygge kontorer i saa mange andre byer som muligt og fremstille varer der. Egen produktion er ikke altid billigere end varer, som I af og til kan koebe billigt. Men egen produktion til fast pris og i fast maengde goer det lettere at regne. Det er for eksempel ideelt til at oprette handelsruter, der stadig forsyner jeres hjemby eller udveksler jeres egne varer mellem to eller flere kontorer.
Men vaer forsigtige med valget af vaerksteder. Taenk grundigt over, hvilke varer byerne faar brug for i fremtiden. Fremstiller I mere, end I kan saelge, bliver overskuddet liggende paa lager, og jeres fortjeneste falder varigt.
Giver jeres egen produktion ingen fortjeneste, saa vaer ikke bange for at lukke eller rive vaerkstedet ned.

column2: Your wealth and your social status are now enough for the rank of Councillor. Now start looking after the well to dos and the rich in your hometown, so that your social welfare status also becomes sufficient.
column3: Jeres formue og jeres anseelse er nu nok til raadmands rang. Tag jer nu af de velstaaende og de rige i jeres hjemby, saa jeres anseelse hos dem ogsaa bliver tilstraekkelig.

column2: Your wealth and social status are now enough for the rank of Councillor. Now start looking after the poor and the well to dos of your hometown, so that your social welfare status also becomes sufficient.
column3: Jeres formue og jeres anseelse er nu nok til raadmands rang. Tag jer nu af de fattige og de velstaaende i jeres hjemby, saa jeres anseelse hos dem ogsaa bliver tilstraekkelig.

column2:
You must gain a much higher status among all citizens of the town within a year, and because you will have to be far richer, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown; then investment increases your wealth and status.
Double or triple your production in Lubeck, and build houses early enough so that the workers and their families can become your tenants. 
Increasing the production also means, that you will have to build new ships in order to transport the products you will produce.
column3:
I skal inden for et aar opnaa en langt hoejere anseelse blandt alle byens borgere, og da I skal vaere langt rigere, boer I investere saa meget som muligt i jeres hjemby, for investeringer oeger formue og anseelse.
Fordobl eller tredobl jeres produktion i Luebeck, og byg huse i god tid, saa arbejderne og deres familier kan blive jeres lejere.
Oeget produktion betyder ogsaa, at I maa bygge nye skibe for at fragte det, I fremstiller.

column2: Above all, you must gain popularity in hometown in order to attain the rank of a Patrician. Once you have attained this, then the office of Lord Mayor will be open to you.\n
column3: Frem for alt maa I vinde popularitet i jeres hjemby for at naa patriciers rang. Naar I har naaet den, staar borgmesterembedet aabent for jer.\n

column2:
In order to become Lord Mayor, you have to surpass the current Lord Mayor in popularity. You are also allowed to surpass other influential citizens of the town.  You can find out if, and where you are, on the candidates list by looking under the rubric "town info" in the council office.
If you have made it to Lord Mayor, you can then strive for the office of Alderman. This is awarded at the Hanse conference. You status in other towns counts for this as well; then all the Hanse towns elect the Chairman of the Hanse. Incidentally, a quick visit to the bathhouse could be helpful.

Good luck.
column3:
For at blive borgmester skal I overgaa den siddende borgmester i popularitet. I skal ogsaa overgaa byens andre indflydelsesrige borgere. Om og hvor I staar paa kandidatlisten, ser I under rubrikken "Byinformation" i raadssalen.
Er I blevet borgmester, kan I straebe efter embedet som oldermand. Det tildeles paa hansedagen. Ogsaa jeres anseelse i andre byer taeller, for alle hansestaeder vaelger Hansaens overhoved. Et besoeg i badstuen kan i oevrigt hjaelpe.

Held og lykke.

column2: June 5th, 1305 - Pope Clement V is elected
column3: 5. juni 1305 - Pave Clemens V vaelges

column2: Bertrand de Got, Archbishop of Bordeaux, is elected Pope in the presence of Philip IV, King of France.
column3: Bertrand de Got, aerkebiskop af Bordeaux, vaelges til pave i naervaer af Filip IV, konge af Frankrig.

column2: 1309 - Pope Clement V relocates his residence to Avignon
column3: 1309 - Pave Clemens V flytter til Avignon

column2: Under pressure from King Philip IV, Pope Clement V relocates the papal residence to Avignon, very much to the anger of the Royal Houses of England and Germany.
column3: Under pres fra kong Filip IV flytter pave Clemens V pavesaedet til Avignon, til stor harme for kongehusene i England og Tyskland.

column2: October 20th, 1314 - Electoral Princes appoint Louis IV King
column3: 20. oktober 1314 - Kurfyrsterne udnaevner Ludvig IV til konge

column2: After the victorious battle against Frederic of Austria, Louis IV of Bavaria is appointed King of Germany.
column3: Efter det sejrrige slag mod Frederik af Oestrig udnaevnes Ludvig IV af Bayern til konge af Tyskland.

column2: August 7th, 1316 - First papal election in Avignon
column3: 7. august 1316 - Foerste pavevalg i Avignon

column2: John XXII is the first pope elected in Avignon. This is the beginning of a power struggle between the Pope and King Louis IV. of Germany.
column3: Johannes XXII er den foerste pave, der vaelges i Avignon. Det er begyndelsen paa en magtkamp mellem paven og kong Ludvig IV af Tyskland.

column2: October 8th, 1323 - The Pope does not recognize King Louis
column3: 8. oktober 1323 - Paven anerkender ikke kong Ludvig

column2: Pope John XXII that of Louis IV abdicate, as he was elected without papal approval and has no valid legitimacy as king.
column3: Pave Johannes XXII kraever, at Ludvig IV abdicerer, da han er valgt uden pavens godkendelse og ikke har gyldig legitimitet som konge.

column2: March 1324 - Louis IV is excommunicated by the Pope
column3: Marts 1324 - Ludvig IV bandlyses af paven

column2: King Louis IV, refusing to abdicate, is excommunicated by the Pope.
column3: Kong Ludvig IV, som naegter at abdicere, bandlyses af paven.

column2: January 29th, 1327 - Edward III becomes King of England
column3: 29. januar 1327 - Edvard III bliver konge af England

column2: Edward III is crowned king at the age of 15. The reign of government, though, is taken over by Lord Roger Mortimer, beloved of Edward's mother Isabella of France.
column3: Edvard III krones til konge som 15-aarig. Regeringen overtages dog af lord Roger Mortimer, elsker af Edvards mor Isabella af Frankrig.

column2: January 11th, 1328 - Ludwig IV receives Imperial crown from the people
column3: 11. januar 1328 - Ludvig IV faar kejserkronen af folket

column2: Louis IV. has himself elected and crowned Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by the people of Rome. Custom demands that he receive the crown from the Pope.
column3: Ludvig IV lader sig vaelge og krone til kejser af Det Tysk-Romerske Rige af Roms folk. Skikken kraever dog, at han faar kronen af paven.

column2: November 1330 - Edward III has Mortimer murdered
column3: November 1330 - Edvard III lader Mortimer myrde

column2: The young King Edward III captures Regent Mortimer and has him assassinated for finally making himself ruler of England.
column3: Den unge kong Edvard III lader regenten Mortimer paagribe og henrette for endelig selv at herske over England.

column2: Dezember 20th, 1334 - New Pope: Benedict XII
column3: 20. december 1334 - Ny pave: Benedikt XII

column2: Pope Benedict XII does not recognize Louis the Bavarian, just as he had done before with his predecessor. Building a new papal palace in Avignon, he also shows his intention of not returning to Rome.
column3: Pave Benedikt XII anerkender ikke Ludvig af Bayern, ligesom hans forgaenger. Ved at bygge et nyt pavepalads i Avignon viser han ogsaa, at han ikke agter at vende tilbage til Rom.

column2: August 4th, 1338 - Louis IV provokes Pope Benedict
column3: 4. august 1338 - Ludvig IV udfordrer pave Benedikt

column2: Louis IV  provokes the Pope once again by declaring that the election of German Kings and their claims for the Imperial Title do not require papal approval.
column3: Ludvig IV udfordrer igen paven ved at erklaere, at valget af tyske konger og deres krav paa kejsertitlen ikke kraever pavens godkendelse.

column2: 1339 - Beginning of the Hundred Years' War
column3: 1339 - Hundredaarskrigen begynder

column2: Edward III of England lays claim to the French Throne, which Philip had inherited. This starts a war which will last over a hundred years.
column3: Edvard III af England goer krav paa Frankrigs trone, som Filip havde arvet. Dermed begynder en krig, der skal vare over hundrede aar.

column2: May 7th, 1342 - Clement VI becomes new Pope
column3: 7. maj 1342 - Clemens VI bliver ny pave

column2: After the death of Pope Benedict XII, Clement VI becomes the new Pope and renews the excommunication of Louis the Bavarian.
column3: Efter pave Benedikt XII's doed bliver Clemens VI ny pave og fornyer bandlysningen af Ludvig af Bayern.

column2: July 11th, 1346 - Charles IV elected king
column3: 11. juli 1346 - Karl IV vaelges til konge

column2: After all sorts of political intrigues, Count Charles IV of Mahren is elected Anti-King in 1346 in preference to the unpopular Louis the Bavarian.
column3: Efter alskens politiske intriger vaelges greve Karl IV af Mähren i 1346 til modkonge i stedet for den upopulaere Ludvig af Bayern.

column2: October 11th, 1347 - Louis the Bavarian dies
column3: 11. oktober 1347 - Ludvig af Bayern doer

column2: King Louis IV, called the Bavarian, dies in the monastery Fürstenfeldbruck. Charles IV is generally recognized as King of Germany.
column3: Kong Ludvig IV, kaldet bayreren, doer ved klostret Fürstenfeldbruck. Karl IV anerkendes alment som konge af Tyskland.

column2: April 7th, 1348 - Founding of the first University in Prague
column3: 7. april 1348 - Foerste universitet grundlaegges i Prag

column2: On 7 April 1348, Charles IV founds the first university of the Holy Roman Empire in Prague. The first university ever founded by Princes was built in Naples in 1224.
column3: Den 7. april 1348 grundlaegger Karl IV i Prag Det Tysk-Romerske Riges foerste universitet. Det allerfoerste universitet grundlagt af en fyrste opstod i Napoli i 1224.

column2: March 3rd, 1349 - Pogroms of Jews in German Towns
column3: 3. marts 1349 - Joedeforfoelgelser i tyske byer

column2: The Jews are made responsible for the Plague. One of the reasons for this is the fact that numerous noble and bourgeois people owe money to the Jews.
column3: Joederne goeres ansvarlige for pesten. En af grundene er, at talrige adelige og borgere skylder joederne penge.

column2: Dezember 18th, 1352 - Innocent VI becomes  Pope
column3: 18. december 1352 - Innocens VI bliver pave

column2: Innocent VI is elected successor to the deceased Pope Clement VI in Avignon. The good relations between the Pope and King Charles are maintained.
column3: Innocens VI vaelges i Avignon som efterfoelger for den afdoede pave Clemens VI. De gode forbindelser mellem paven og kong Karl bestaar.

column2: April 5th, 1355 - Charles IV is elected Emperor
column3: 5. april 1355 - Karl IV vaelges til kejser

column2: On his journey through Italy, King Charles IV has himself appointed Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by a papal nuncio.
column3: Paa sin rejse gennem Italien lader kong Karl IV sig udnaevne til kejser af Det Tysk-Romerske Rige af en pavelig legat.

column2: January 10th, 1356 - Golden Bulle forbids the alliance of towns
column3: 10. januar 1356 - Den Gyldne Bulle forbyder byforbund

column2: On the Reichstag in Nuremberg, King Karl IV declares the "Goldene Bulle. One regulation among others prohibits the alliance of towns.
column3: Paa rigsdagen i Nürnberg udsteder kong Karl IV "Den Gyldne Bulle". En af bestemmelserne forbyder byforbund.

column2: October 14th, 1360 - Peace between England and France
column3: 14. oktober 1360 - Fred mellem England og Frankrig

column2: France and England make a peace-contract in Calais. Edward III renounces the French Crown. In return, territories in France are granted to him.
column3: Frankrig og England slutter fred i Calais. Edvard III giver afkald paa den franske krone. Til gengaeld faar han landomraader i Frankrig.

column2: January 16th, 1362 - Storm-tide on the North sea
column3: 16. januar 1362 - Stormflod i Nordsoeen

column2: De grote Mandränke, an enormous storm tide rages at the coast of North Friesland. The mainland is torn apart into separate islands.
column3: De grote Mandränke, en vaeldig stormflod, raser langs Nordfrislands kyst. Fastlandet rives itu i adskilte oeer.

column2: November 1367 - The Pope returns to Rome
column3: November 1367 - Paven vender tilbage til Rom

column2: In 1367, under pressure from Charles IV, Pope Urban V relocates the residence of the Church from Avignon to Rome.
column3: I 1367 flytter pave Urban V under pres fra Karl IV kirkens saede fra Avignon til Rom.

column2: 1368 - Charles IV on second Italian journey
column3: 1368 - Karl IV's anden italienske rejse

column2: King Charles IV starts his second journey to Italy, thus supporting the return of Pope Urban V to Rome.
column3: Kong Karl IV begynder sin anden rejse til Italien og stoetter dermed pave Urban V's tilbagevenden til Rom.

column2: March 28th, 1369 - New outbreak of war
column3: 28. marts 1369 - Krigen blusser op igen

column2: The Hundred Years' War between England and France breaks out once again.
column3: Hundredaarskrigen mellem England og Frankrig bryder ud paa ny.

column2: September 24th, 1370 - Unrest drives the Pope out of Rome
column3: 24. september 1370 - Uroligheder driver paven fra Rom

column2: Pope Urban V flies from Rome due to unrest and returns to Avignon. He dies there a short time later.
column3: Pave Urban V flygter fra Rom paa grund af uroligheder og vender tilbage til Avignon. Han doer der kort efter.

column2: June 5th, 1372 - Naval battle at La Rochelle
column3: 5. juni 1372 - Soeslaget ved La Rochelle

column2: A fleet of Castilians, being allied with France, severely defeat England in the naval battle at La Rochelle.
column3: En kastiliansk flaade i forbund med Frankrig tilfoejer England et haardt nederlag i soeslaget ved La Rochelle.

column2: October 20th, 1375 - Charles IV visits Lubeck
column3: 20. oktober 1375 - Karl IV besoeger Luebeck

column2: Charles IV, Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, visits Lubeck and recognizes the importance of the town by nobly addressing the Patricians with: "Gentlemen".
column3: Karl IV, kejser af Det Tysk-Romerske Rige, besoeger Luebeck og anerkender byens betydning ved aedelt at tiltale patricierne med "Mine herrer".

column2: January 1377 - Pope returns to Rome
column3: Januar 1377 - Paven vender tilbage til Rom

column2: Under Pope Gregory XI, the Head of the Catholic Church finally returns to Rome, after having resided in Avignon since 1309.
column3: Under pave Gregor XI vender den katolske kirkes overhoved endelig tilbage til Rom efter at have resideret i Avignon siden 1309.

column2: April 9th, 1378 - Papal election in Rome
column3: 9. april 1378 - Pavevalg i Rom

column2: Pressured by the people, Urban VI, an Italian, is elected Pope, succeeding the deceased Gregory XI.
column3: Under pres fra folket vaelges italieneren Urban VI til pave som efterfoelger for den afdoede Gregor XI.

column2: September 17th, 1384 - Butchers uprising
column3: 17. september 1384 - Slagteroproeret

column2: The uprising of butcher's in Lubeck is quashed. Like many other trade guilds, the butchers reject the reign of the Patricians in the town council.
column3: Slagternes oproer i Luebeck slaas ned. Som mange andre lav afviser slagterne patriciernes styre i byraadet.

column2: 1390 - First paper mill in Germany
column3: 1390 - Foerste papirmoelle i Tyskland

column2: The first sheets of paper in Germany are produced in Nuremberg. Spanish Moors brought this Chinese invention to Europe for the first time in 1150.
column3: I Nürnberg fremstilles Tysklands foerste papirark. Spanske maurere bragte denne kinesiske opfindelse til Europa allerede i 1150.

column2: November 11th, 1417 - The Schism comes to an end
column3: 11. november 1417 - Skismaet ophoerer

column2: The competing Popes, John XXIII and Gregory XII, are pressured to abdicate and make way for the election of Pope Martin V. The Church's schism ends after 39 years.
column3: De rivaliserende paver Johannes XXIII og Gregor XII tvinges til at abdicere for at give plads for valget af pave Martin V. Kirkens skisma ophoerer efter 39 aar.

column2: May 7th, 1429 - Joan of Arc in Orleans
column3: 7. maj 1429 - Jeanne d'Arc i Orléans

column2: Orleans, which has been under siege by  English troops for months, is liberated by French soldiers led by the peasant girl Joan of Arc.
column3: Orléans, der i maaneder har vaeret belejret af engelske tropper, befries af franske soldater anfoert af bondepigen Jeanne d'Arc.

column2: May 30th, 1431 - Joan of Arc to be burnt
column3: 30. maj 1431 - Jeanne d'Arc paa baalet

column2: In Rouen, Joanne of Arc is accused of heresy by the English and burnt. The war between France and England ages on.
column3: I Rouen anklages Jeanne d'Arc for kaetteri af englaenderne og braendes. Krigen mellem Frankrig og England raser videre.

column2: 1453 - Hundred Years' War ends
column3: 1453 - Hundredaarskrigen slutter

column2: After the victory of King Charles VII of France over the English troops at Castillon, the war which had started in 1339 comes to an end.
column3: Efter kong Karl VII af Frankrigs sejr over de engelske tropper ved Castillon slutter krigen, der begyndte i 1339.

column2: August 1456 - The Gutenberg Bible is published
column3: August 1456 - Gutenbergbiblen udkommer

column2: The first printed bible with over 1.200 pages and an edition of 180 pieces is published in Mainz. Gutenberg had invented the printing of books in 1445.
column3: I Mainz udkommer den foerste trykte bibel med over 1.200 sider i et oplag paa 180 eksemplarer. Gutenberg havde opfundet bogtrykkerkunsten i 1445.

column2: October 12th, 1492 - Discovery of America
column3: 12. oktober 1492 - Amerika opdages

column2: Christopher Columbus reaches the island of San Salvador with three ships and officially takes possession of it for Spain. At first, he misguidedly thought that he had discovered the much sought after sea route to India.
column3: Christoffer Columbus naar med tre skibe oeen San Salvador og tager den officielt i besiddelse for Spanien. Foerst tror han fejlagtigt at have fundet den eftertragtede soevej til Indien.

column2: October 31th, 1517 - 95 theses against the selling of indulgences
column3: 31. oktober 1517 - 95 teser mod afladshandlen

column2: Martin Luther reads out 95 theses against the selling of indulgences at the castle church of Wittenberg. As a result, the division of the Churches develops in the course of the following years.
column3: Martin Luther offentliggoer ved slotskirken i Wittenberg 95 teser mod afladshandlen. I de foelgende aar foerer det til kirkens splittelse.

column2: May 24th, 1543 - Nicolaus Copernicus dies
column3: 24. maj 1543 - Nicolaus Copernicus doer

column2: Nicolaus Copernicus, born in Thorn, publishes his works on the solar system only a short time before his death. In this work he presents the opinion that the sun, not the Earth, is the fixed center of the solar system.
column3: Nicolaus Copernicus, foedt i Thorn, udgiver sit vaerk om solsystemet kort foer sin doed. Heri haevder han, at solen og ikke jorden er solsystemets faste midtpunkt.

column3: I 1669 holdes den sidste officielle hansedag i Luebeck. Kun 9 tyske hansestaeder deltager, blandt dem Bremen, Hamburg og Luebeck.

column2: Good luck!
column3: Held og lykke!

column2:
My dear Son!

You are old enough to tread in my footsteps, but first of all you should gain your own experiences.

Before I, because of my political obligations, settled down in Lubeck and married your mother, I was a travelling hawker and captain of a proud snaikka, and at home throughout the whole area of the Hanse. I would like you to follow my footsteps and gain admission to Hanse through your own resources. As start-up capital you are getting nothing more than a snaikka, a trading office in Lubeck, so that we can get to see you from time to time, and some cash. It should be easy enough to make it to a trader with this.

Your loving father

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaere soen!

Du er gammel nok til at traede i mine fodspor, men foerst boer du goere dine egne erfaringer.

Foer jeg paa grund af mine politiske forpligtelser slog mig ned i Luebeck og giftede mig med din mor, var jeg omvandrende kraemmer og kaptajn paa en stolt snekke, hjemme i hele Hansaens omraade. Jeg vil gerne, at du foelger i mine fodspor og vinder indpas i Hansaen ved egen kraft. Som startkapital faar du intet andet end en snekke, et kontor i Luebeck, saa vi kan se dig af og til, og nogle rede penge. Dermed burde det vaere let nok at blive handelsmand.

Din kaerlige far

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Dangers
column3: Farer

column2:
My dear Son!

You have indeed enjoyed an excellent education, and one in which you could count the cleverest brains in Europe as your tutors, but so far you have never left the mainland.
So let me give you some good advice on the way: Be careful of  "travelling hawkers" in the same way, as you should be of the ship's kobold! There are many dangers awaiting you on the wide-open oceans, but this ghost ship is a monstrous creation of the devil himself. 

God protect you!
P.S. Your mother worries about you, so do not be too boisterous in your youthful high spirits!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaere soen!

Du har ganske vist nydt en fremragende opdragelse, med Europas klogeste hoveder som laerere, men du har endnu aldrig forladt fastlandet.
Lad mig derfor give dig et godt raad med paa vejen: tag dig lige saa meget i agt for "omvandrende handelsmaend" som for skibsnissen! Mange farer venter dig paa de vide have, men dette spoegelsesskib er et uhyrligt vaerk af djaevelen selv.

Gud bevare dig!
P.S. Din mor er bekymret for dig, saa vaer ikke for vild i din ungdommelige overmod!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Illness
column3: Sygdom

column2:
My dear Son!

I observe with joy how well your business is flourishing. If you continue in this way, then you will easily make it to trader and way above that.

However, think not only about your own personal financial profit, but also about the needs of the people with whom you trade in the towns! Do not forget; wealth causes loneliness!

There is also a sad reason for my writing to you, your mother is not well, she has been in bed with high fever for days now, and the best doctors in the Hanse are at a lost as to what sort of rare illness it might be. I am sending to Florence for a doctor; hopefully, he will arrive in time!

Loving greetings, from your mother as well. And take care of yourself.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaere soen!

Med glaede ser jeg, hvor godt dine forretninger blomstrer. Fortsaetter du saadan, bliver du let handelsmand og langt mere.

Men taenk ikke kun paa din egen vinding, men ogsaa paa behovene hos de mennesker, du handler med i byerne! Glem ikke: rigdom goer ensom!

Jeg skriver ogsaa af en soergelig grund: din mor har det ikke godt, hun har ligget i dagevis med hoej feber, og Hansaens bedste laeger ved ikke, hvad for en sjaelden sygdom det kan vaere. Jeg har sendt bud efter en laege fra Firenze; gid han naar frem i tide!

Kaerlige hilsner, ogsaa fra din mor. Og pas paa dig selv.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Joy and sorrow
column3: Glaede og sorg

column2:
My Dear Son!

Why must joy and sorrow always have to be so close together?  I had hardly said goodbye to the Lord Mayor, who told me about your imminent appointment to trader, when master Ardovini summoned me. In my last letter to you, I spoke about this famous doctor. He arrived in Lubeck two weeks ago, but not even he was able to treat your mother's puzzling illness. She died suddenly two days ago, after her condition had remained stable for a long time and the hope of her recovering had begun to grow. Her body will be put to rest in the crypt in Lubeck next Sunday. And I feel the ravages of time nibbling at me in an above average way.

In spite of this gloomy news, please accept my best wishes on your quick advancement!

Your loving father

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaere soen!

Hvorfor skal glaede og sorg altid ligge saa taet sammen? Knap havde jeg taget afsked med borgmesteren, der fortalte mig om din forestaaende udnaevnelse til handelsmand, foer mester Ardovini lod mig kalde. I mit sidste brev skrev jeg om denne beroemte laege. Han kom til Luebeck for to uger siden, men end ikke han kunne helbrede din mors gaadefulde sygdom. Hun doede pludselig for to dage siden, efter at hendes tilstand laenge havde vaeret stabil og haabet om bedring var begyndt at vokse. Hendes legeme bisaettes i krypten i Luebeck paa soendag. Og jeg maerker tidens tand gnave i mig mere end ellers.

Trods disse dystre nyheder skal du have mine bedste oensker for din hurtige forfremmelse!

Din kaerlige far

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Travelling merchant
column3: Rejsende koebmand

column2:
Dear Leopold!

It is now hardly a week ago since I last wrote to you.  I buried your mother yesterday. You are now the only one that I have left.

God have mercy on my sinful soul, and do not let me loose you as well! You are a prudent trader, and I am sure that you won't disappoint me. Enclosed with this letter I am sending you 50,000\C, to speed up your career.

As soon as you have made it to a long distance merchant, I will tell you a secret that has been a burden on my conscience for a long time.Do not ask me about it, I can't tell you about it yet. In any case, not before I am certain that... No!  Go away, I told you that, I wouldn't betray it...

\f1_Young Sir!

Your father has asked me to give you this letter. The death of his wife has hit him so hard, that he fantasises from time to time even when he has all his wits about him. He is, however, significantly better and you need not worry about him.

On behalf of my charitable Mr. George Jantzen

\f3_Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Kaere Leopold!

Det er knap en uge siden, jeg sidst skrev til dig. I gaar begravede jeg din mor. Nu er du den eneste, jeg har tilbage.

Gud vaere min syndige sjael naadig, og lad mig ikke miste ogsaa dig! Du er en klog handelsmand, og jeg er sikker paa, at du ikke skuffer mig. Med dette brev sender jeg dig 50.000\C for at fremskynde din loebebane.

Saa snart du er blevet fjernhandelsmand, vil jeg fortaelle dig en hemmelighed, der laenge har tynget min samvittighed. Spoerg mig ikke om den, jeg kan ikke fortaelle den endnu. I hvert fald ikke foer jeg er sikker paa, at... Nej! Gaa vaek, jeg har jo sagt, at jeg ikke vil forraade det...

\f1_Unge herre!

Jeres far har bedt mig give jer dette brev. Hans hustrus doed har ramt ham saa haardt, at han af og til taler i vildelse, selv naar han er ved sine fulde fem. Han har det dog betydeligt bedre, og I behoever ikke bekymre jer om ham.

Paa vegne af min velgoerer, hr. Georg Jantzen

\f3_Jeres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Marriage
column3: Aegteskab

column2:
My dear Son,

My apologies for the last letter; the excitement of the last few weeks was simply too much for me. Lets face it; I am not the youngest anymore. You, on the other hand, have your whole life in front of you. And even though you are perhaps not thinking about it at the moment, I would still like to give you a piece of advice.

I am speaking about marriage, taking a friendly woman into the harbour of wedlock. And my good advice on it is as follows: Look for a good and mild-spirited woman, one, who is kind to the poor. That would be good for your social standing and peace of mind, and even the ship's kobold agrees favourably.

God protect you!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaere soen,

Tilgiv mig mit sidste brev; de sidste ugers ophidselse var mig simpelthen for meget. Lad os indroemme det: jeg er ikke den yngste laengere. Du derimod har hele livet foran dig. Og selv om du maaske ikke taenker paa det lige nu, vil jeg alligevel give dig et raad.

Jeg taler om aegteskabet, om at foere en venlig kvinde ind i aegtestandens havn. Og mit gode raad lyder: soeg en god og mild kvinde, som er venlig mod de fattige. Det ville vaere godt for din anseelse og din sjaelefred, og selv skibsnissen ville se det med milde oejne.

Gud bevare dig!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Sorrows
column3: Bekymringer

column2:
Young Sir,

I am seriously worried about your father. In recent times, he has been waking up increasingly from dreadful dreams during the nights, and calls, as if in madness, for your dead mother and the priest. 
Indeed, he has infrequently had these nightmares in the past, but never with such intensity.

Besides that, he has refused to leave the house or let anyone else in, besides the priest. He has even given the order not to let you in unless you have been awarded the title of merchant. In his present state of mind, he is quite capable of throwing you out of the house without this title.

I am writing this letter without his knowledge and beg you, as soon as you can fulfil his wish, to quickly come and see your father.

Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Jeg er alvorligt bekymret for jeres far. Paa det seneste vaagner han stadig oftere om natten af forfaerdelige droemme og raaber, som i vanvid, paa jeres afdoede mor og praesten.
Ganske vist har han foer af og til haft saadanne mareridt, men aldrig saa voldsomt.

Desuden naegter han at forlade huset eller lukke nogen ind, bortset fra praesten. Han har endog givet ordre til ikke at lukke jer ind, foer I har faaet titlen koebmand. I sin nuvaerende sindstilstand er han fuldt i stand til at smide jer ud uden denne titel.

Jeg skriver dette brev uden hans vidende og beder jer om, saa snart I kan opfylde hans oenske, hurtigt at komme til jeres far.

Jeres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Father's death
column3: Faderens doed

column2:
Young Sir!

It is my sad duty to report this tragedy to you. Your father passed away last night His aging heart could no longer cope with the constant excitement, and he had not had a peaceful night's sleep for weeks.What dreadful pain of fate, so close to the fulfilment of his most ardent desire, your appearing in front of him as a merchant.
You father will at least receive a funeral befitting his status. The news of his death is spreading like bush fire through the town, and the citizens of Lubeck are remembering the charitable deeds, which he did for the town. And he, who did not experience how Lubeck visibly flourished during his term of office as Lord Mayor, now hears about it on every street corner.
The name of your family is once again on every tongue, then until recently, only a few remembered how much their own careers owed to your father's support. I shouldn't be surprised if some of this euphoria is not transferred to your person.

Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Det er min soergelige pligt at meddele jer denne ulykke. Jeres far gik bort i nat. Hans aldrende hjerte kunne ikke laengere klare den stadige ophidselse, og han havde ikke haft en rolig nats soevn i ugevis. Hvilken grusom skaebne, saa taet paa opfyldelsen af hans inderligste oenske: at se jer traede frem for ham som koebmand.
Jeres far faar i det mindste en begravelse, der soemmer sig for hans stand. Nyheden om hans doed spreder sig som en loebeild gennem byen, og Luebecks borgere mindes de velgerninger, han gjorde for byen. Og han, som ikke oplevede, hvordan Luebeck synligt blomstrede i hans tid som borgmester, hoerer nu om det paa hvert gadehjoerne.
Jeres slaegts navn er igen paa alles laeber, hvor indtil for nylig kun faa huskede, hvor meget deres egne loebebaner skyldte jeres fars stoette. Det ville ikke undre mig, om noget af denne begejstring gik over paa jeres person.

Jeres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Nightmares
column3: Mareridt

column2:
Young Sir!

My best wishes on your speedy career. Your father's affairs are taking their usual course. After the very deeply touching funeral, in which the whole of Lubeck took part, notaries, court officials and other civil servants are now moving in to regulate your father's estate. I will keep you informed so far as this is concerned.

However, concerning your father's secret, which he has now taken with him to the grave, I will now tell you what I know about it. I do not think he would be against it, now that you are a recognised merchant.
Unfortunately I can only tell you this much, it must have something to do with a "travelling trader", who your father always fantasises about in his sleep. Late in the evenings, when I took tea to him in the smoking room, he was sometimes already asleep, tossing and turning, on the couch. That's when I heard this name.
These nightmares must go back to an experience that he had as a young man at sea. Your father stayed in contact with a comrade from those days. Perhaps it will be possible for me to find out his whereabouts. I will then write you again.
column3:
Unge herre!

Mine bedste oensker for jeres hurtige loebebane. Jeres fars anliggender gaar deres vante gang. Efter den dybt bevaegende begravelse, som hele Luebeck deltog i, er notarer, retsbetjente og andre embedsmaend nu i gang med at ordne jeres fars doedsbo. Jeg holder jer underrettet om dette.

Hvad angaar jeres fars hemmelighed, som han nu har taget med sig i graven, vil jeg fortaelle, hvad jeg ved. Jeg tror ikke, han ville have noget imod det, nu da I er en anerkendt koebmand.
Desvaerre kan jeg kun sige saa meget, at det maa have med en "omvandrende handelsmand" at goere, som jeres far altid taler i vildelse om i soevne. Sent om aftenen, naar jeg bragte ham te i rygevaerelset, sov han af og til allerede og kastede sig frem og tilbage paa sofaen. Det var da, jeg hoerte dette navn.
Disse mareridt maa gaa tilbage til noget, han oplevede paa havet som ung mand. Jeres far holdt kontakt med en kammerat fra dengang. Maaske lykkes det mig at finde ud af, hvor han opholder sig. Saa skriver jeg til jer igen.

column2: Steersman
column3: Styrmand

column2:
Young Sir!

I have looked in your father's personal records to try and find out the whereabouts of his old comrade, who I wrote to you about. It wasn't very easy to get hold of these documents, because the authorities are carrying out a strict investigation of the entire estate. But I found out something about this old comrade:
Jakob Blank was the helmsman on your father's snaikka for many years and afterwards became his companion. He later became a councillor in Riga, where he presumable still lives. He was a regular guest in Lubeck, but not in the last few years. This however, is the best evidence that I could find. Look for a certain Jakob Blank in Riga or the "Helmsman" as he is also called!

Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Jeg har ledt i jeres fars personlige papirer for at finde ud af, hvor hans gamle kammerat, som jeg skrev om, opholder sig. Det var ikke let at faa fat i disse dokumenter, for myndighederne gennemfoerer en streng undersoegelse af hele doedsboet. Men jeg fandt ud af noget om denne gamle kammerat:
Jakob Blank var i mange aar styrmand paa jeres fars snekke og blev siden hans kompagnon. Senere blev han raadmand i Riga, hvor han formentlig stadig bor. Han var en hyppig gaest i Luebeck, men ikke de seneste aar. Dette er dog det bedste spor, jeg kunne finde. Soeg efter en vis Jakob Blank i Riga, eller "Styrmanden", som han ogsaa kaldes!

Jeres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Condolence
column3: Kondolence

column2:
My dear Leopold!

You have certainly never heard about me, but I was a close acquaintance of your father and I have carefully followed your career. Be certain of my condolences in respect of the sudden and unexpected death of old Georg. If you are ever in need of anything, be assured that you can turn to me in confidence. 

Greeting from the free town of Bremen
Patrician H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Min kaere Leopold!

I har sikkert aldrig hoert om mig, men jeg var en naer bekendt af jeres far og har noeje fulgt jeres loebebane. Vaer forvisset om min deltagelse i gamle Georgs pludselige og uventede doed. Skulle I nogensinde faa brug for noget, saa vid, at I trygt kan henvende jer til mig.

Hilsen fra den frie by Bremen
Patricier H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Classified document
column3: Hemmeligt dokument

column2:
Honourable {%R:04} Jantzen!

You have made inquires in Riga about a certain Jakob Blank. Let me give you some good advice: Forget this name and return to Lubeck!
I already suspect that you won't follow this advice, I am therefore giving you the official statement that the matter Jakob Blank has been declared top secret on the orders of the Hanse convention. Nobody will give you any information about the darkest hour in the history of this town.
The only course of action would be for another Hanse town to make an official request to Riga. But you must bear the rank of a councillor in order to do so. And even then, you will have to have gained a certain status in Riga before I would respond to your request. These strict rules have been approved by the Hanse Authority and are thought of only as security measures.As soon as these conditions have been fulfilled, I will announce what you want to know.

The Lord Mayor 
{%+:0B}
column3:
Aerede {%R:04} Jantzen!

I har gjort forespoergsler i Riga om en vis Jakob Blank. Lad mig give jer et godt raad: glem dette navn og vend tilbage til Luebeck!
Jeg aner allerede, at I ikke vil foelge dette raad, og giver jer derfor den officielle meddelelse, at sagen Jakob Blank paa hansedagens befaling er erklaeret hemmelig. Ingen vil give jer oplysninger om den moerkeste time i denne bys historie.
Den eneste vej ville vaere, at en anden hansestad retter en officiel henvendelse til Riga. Men dertil skal I baere raadmands rang. Og selv da maa I have opnaaet en vis anseelse i Riga, foer jeg vil besvare jeres henvendelse. Disse strenge regler er godkendt af hansedagen og er udelukkende taenkt som forsigtighedsregler. Saa snart disse betingelser er opfyldt, vil jeg meddele, hvad I oensker at vide.

Borgmesteren

column2:
Concerning the request of Leopold Jantzen from Lubeck, in the matter of the ostracised Jakob Blank

The following announcement is issued:

The person Jakob Blank was banned from Riga for lifetime over 15 years ago, for endangering the security of the town and for 20 other crimes.
On the orders of the Hanse Authority, all Hanse towns were sent a request, demanding support for this sentence.
His last known place of residence is Oslo.
This information is confidential and for official use only.

The Lord Mayor
{%+:0B}
column3:
Angaaende Leopold Jantzen fra Luebecks henvendelse i sagen om den fredloese Jakob Blank

Foelgende bekendtgoeres:

Personen Jakob Blank blev for mere end 15 aar siden forvist fra Riga paa livstid for at have bragt byens sikkerhed i fare og for 20 andre forbrydelser.
Paa hansedagens befaling blev der sendt en anmodning til alle hansestaeder om at stoette denne dom.
Hans sidst kendte opholdssted er Oslo.
Denne oplysning er fortrolig og kun til tjenestebrug.

Borgmesteren

I stikker naesen i ting, som I gjorde bedst i at holde jer fra. Tag det som et godt raad venner imellem.

column2: Guild help
column3: Lavets hjaelp

column2:
Honourable {%R:04} Jantzen! 

I have seen you questioning the people in the markets and the narrow streets of Oslo. This aroused my attention; then such behaviour is not befitting to a man of your rank.
As I have been told, you are looking for Jakob Blank. This poor beggar was taken for a ride by your "fine" society and came to us for protection in order to disappear unnoticed. Pardon! I forgot to introduce myself. My name is really not of any significance, suffice to say, that I chair the local guild. I am sure you understand what I mean, and whilst not wanting to appear too arrogant - I do not indeed, look like a vagabond. 
We took Jakob Blank away into a secure country area at the time, and the colleagues there did such a good job that not even I can say where he is at the moment. But I would certainly have heard of his death. 
Because you appear to be his friend, I will support you in your inquires. For me to do that, you will have to acquire a reputation of trust in the community otherwise I won't be able to do anything for you. When your name becomes known in the right circles, you will get the required information almost automatically.

Farewell,
\f5_X
column3:
Aerede {%R:04} Jantzen!

Jeg har set jer udspoerge folk paa torvene og i Oslos smalle gader. Det vakte min opmaerksomhed, for en saadan opfoersel soemmer sig ikke for en mand af jeres rang.
Som jeg har hoert, leder I efter Jakob Blank. Denne stakkels fyr blev narret af jeres "fine" selskab og kom til os for at faa beskyttelse og forsvinde ubemaerket. Undskyld! Jeg glemte at praesentere mig. Mit navn er virkelig uden betydning; lad det vaere nok at sige, at jeg er formand for det stedlige lav. I forstaar sikkert, hvad jeg mener, og uden at ville virke for hovmodig - jeg ligner jo ikke en landstryger.
Vi bragte dengang Jakob Blank til en sikker egn, og kollegerne der gjorde saa godt et arbejde, at ikke engang jeg kan sige, hvor han er nu. Men om hans doed ville jeg helt sikkert have hoert.
Da I synes at vaere hans ven, vil jeg stoette jer i jeres eftersoegning. Dertil maa I vinde faellesskabets tillid, ellers kan jeg intet goere for jer. Naar jeres navn bliver kendt i de rette kredse, faar I de noedvendige oplysninger naesten af sig selv.

Farvel,
\f5_X

column2:
Dear Leopold Jantzen!

I have made so much effort to leave the misfortunes of the past behind me. However, when I heard about the death of your father, I knew that you would be looking for me and that my old debt had caught up with me again.
I am sure you have come to ask me about the  "flying trader". I will tell you what I know, but before that you'll have to do something for me.
Take me to grave of my old friend in Lubeck so that I can pray for his and my eternal soul!
I will wait on your ship {%s:09} for you.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kaere Leopold Jantzen!

Jeg har gjort saa meget for at laegge fortidens ulykker bag mig. Men da jeg hoerte om jeres fars doed, vidste jeg, at I ville lede efter mig, og at min gamle skyld igen havde indhentet mig.
I er sikkert kommet for at spoerge mig om "Den flyvende handelsmand". Jeg vil fortaelle, hvad jeg ved, men foerst maa I goere noget for mig.
Foer mig til min gamle vens grav i Luebeck, saa jeg kan bede for hans og min evige sjael!
Jeg venter paa jer paa jeres skib {%s:09}.

Jakob Blank

column2: Inheritance
column3: Arv

column2:
Announcement of the decision concerning the estate of the Lubecker citizen and Patrician, Georg Jantzen.

On the basis of an old document that was stored in the archives of Bremen and Lubeck, the officials of the said towns, have jointly come to the following agreement:

As agreed in writing at the time, the Bremer Patrician Vanderdeeken inherits the estate of the Jantzens of Lubeck. Besides monies, the assets also include movables and immovable, such as ships and buildings.

Other assets to be transferred include the forenamed values of the  {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen, where it can be proved that a substantial part of it came from his father's estate. 
The transfer will take place in five days.

{%+:01}
column3:
Bekendtgoerelse af beslutningen om doedsboet efter Luebeck-borgeren og patricieren Georg Jantzen.

Paa grundlag af et gammelt dokument, der blev opbevaret i arkiverne i Bremen og Luebeck, er embedsmaendene i de naevnte byer i faellesskab naaet til foelgende ordning:

Som dengang aftalt skriftligt arver patricieren Vanderdeeken fra Bremen familien Jantzens bo i Luebeck. Ud over penge omfatter formuen ogsaa loesoere og fast ejendom, saasom skibe og bygninger.

Til den formue, der skal overdrages, hoerer desuden de foernaevnte vaerdier tilhoerende {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen, for saa vidt det kan paavises, at en vaesentlig del stammer fra hans fars bo.
Overdragelsen finder sted om fem dage.

{%+:01}

column2: Stranger
column3: Fremmed

column2:
Dear Sir!

A peculiar stranger was inquiring about you in the harbour area of {%t:08}. He was wearing a long black habit, and his appearance sent shivers down my spine.
However, because you are waiting for an urgent message, whose source is not so important, I have sent the stranger to you.

Greetings,Sailor {%V:0F} from {%s:09}
column3:
Herre!

En underlig fremmed har spurgt efter jer i havnen i {%t:08}. Han bar en lang sort kutte, og hans udseende fik det til at loebe mig koldt ned ad ryggen.
Men da I venter paa et hastende budskab, hvis oprindelse ikke er saa vigtig, har jeg sendt den fremmede til jer.

Hilsen, matros {%V:0F} paa {%s:09}

column2: Offer
column3: Tilbud

column2:
Leopold Jantzen!

It is wonderful to personally make your acquaintance. I knew your father, a very pleasant person - until he fell victim to madness. I hear you are looking for Jakob Blank. Yet another acquaintance of mine, unfortunately I do not even know myself, where he is at the moment.But I have been observing you for a while now. You are someone who could go quite far; I can feel something like that immediately. You only need a little support from the side of influence. I can offer you this support. You'll see, with me working for you in the background everything will develop to your advantage. Without me, however, some wishes are unattainable. I'll give you the choice:

Do you want to become rich and famous with me? Or do you want to risk being crushed between the millstones of intrigue if you pursue the rough road to the summit?
What I demand for my support is nothing more than a fair share of your future wealth. Decide wisely!
column3:
Leopold Jantzen!

Det er en fornoejelse at stifte jeres personlige bekendtskab. Jeg kendte jeres far, et meget behageligt menneske - indtil han faldt som offer for vanviddet. Jeg hoerer, at I leder efter Jakob Blank. Endnu en af mine bekendte; desvaerre ved jeg ikke engang selv, hvor han er lige nu. Men jeg har iagttaget jer et stykke tid. I er en, der kan naa langt; saadan noget maerker jeg straks. I mangler blot lidt stoette fra indflydelsesrig side. Den stoette kan jeg tilbyde jer. I skal se: med mig virkende for jer i baggrunden vil alt udvikle sig til jeres fordel. Uden mig forbliver visse oensker derimod uopnaaelige. Jeg giver jer valget:

Vil I blive rig og beroemt med mig? Eller vil I risikere at blive knust mellem intrigernes moellesten, hvis I gaar den barske vej mod toppen?
Hvad jeg kraever for min stoette, er intet andet end en rimelig andel af jeres fremtidige rigdom. Vaelg klogt!

Your rejection of this generous offer offends me. You alone will bear the responsibility for this decision. I did warn you!

Farewell!

Jeres afvisning af dette gavmilde tilbud kraenker mig. I alene baerer ansvaret for denne beslutning. Jeg advarede jer!

Leopold Jantzen!

Your decision was clever and will make you into a rich and powerful man. You must in fact pay for a few of your father's mistakes but after that, nothing will hold you back.
You will hear from again when the time is right.

Until then.
column3:
Leopold Jantzen!

Jeres beslutning var klog og vil goere jer til en rig og maegtig mand. Ganske vist maa I betale for nogle af jeres fars fejltrin, men derefter vil intet holde jer tilbage.
I vil hoere fra mig igen, naar tiden er inde.

Indtil da.

column2: Generous
column3: Gavmild

column2:
Poor Leopold!

You will certainly be surprised over the change in circumstances and disappointed over your own poverty. But, how should you have known what agreements the good old Georg was capable of entering into, just to further his career.
I said that we were old acquaintances, your father and I, and although he always looked down at me, I now feel almost sorry for you in your situation - To be cheated of what one has built up by ones own father. Whilst I'm in a good mood, I'll let you have something from the estate that now legally belongs to me. I do not need a second trading office in Lubeck, and I now really have a surplus of ships and small change.
You do not have to thank me for my generosity, just simply stay out of my way in future.

H. Vanderdeeken
