column3:
Stakkels Leopold!

I er sikkert overrasket over de aendrede forhold og skuffet over jeres egen fattigdom. Men hvordan skulle I have vidst, hvilke aftaler gode gamle Georg var i stand til at indgaa, blot for at fremme sin loebebane?
Jeg sagde jo, at vi var gamle bekendte, jeres far og jeg, og selv om han altid saa ned paa mig, har jeg nu naesten ondt af jer i jeres situation - at blive bestjaalet af sin egen far for det, man selv har bygget op. Da jeg er i godt humoer, lader jeg jer faa noget af det bo, der nu retmaessigt tilhoerer mig. Jeg har ikke brug for et andet kontor i Luebeck, og skibe og smaapenge har jeg sandelig i overflod.
I behoever ikke takke mig for min gavmildhed; hold jer blot ude af min vej i fremtiden.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Home journey
column3: Hjemrejse

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

I prayed at the grave of your father for both of our souls. I now feel strong enough to tell you about the "flying trader", however not here in Lubeck.
The curse, which hung over your father, is even effective beyond the grave and affects the whole family. My luck that I never married.
Take me back to Stetin! I will satisfy your inquisitiveness in my home.
I will again wait for you in the harbour tavern.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg har bedt ved jeres fars grav for vore begges sjaele. Nu foeler jeg mig staerk nok til at fortaelle om "Den flyvende handelsmand", men ikke her i Luebeck.
Den forbandelse, der hvilede over jeres far, virker endog ud over graven og rammer hele slaegten. Heldigt for mig, at jeg aldrig blev gift.
Foer mig tilbage til Stettin! I mit hjem vil jeg stille jeres nysgerrighed.
Jeg venter igen paa jer paa havnekroen.

Jakob Blank

column2: Devil ship
column3: Djaevleskib

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

Thank you for the safe journey home! As promised, I will now tell you about the journey on which your father and I met the  "flying trader".
I'm sure you have already heard the story of the  "flying trader", haven't you? The "flying trader" is a ghost ship that wanders the North and Baltic Seas. Its captain was a greedy trader who went into consorts with the devil to increase his fortune. And he amassed a great fortune, which he jealously guarded on his huge ship.
One day however, the devil demanded the return of his share, but the mean trader refused to pay.
The devil laughed at him, he would get his own back.  He dammed the trader never to leave his ship full of gold, and in addition to that, never to find a place of rest until the end of time.  The  "flying trader" has been sailing the Northern Seas with his ghost ship ever since then and brings misfortunes to seamen who come across his ship.
That's enough for today, as you can see, my hands are shaking from recalling the story. Let me rest for a day and I will then tell you the rest of the story.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kaere unge Jantzen!

Tak for den sikre hjemrejse! Som lovet vil jeg nu fortaelle om den rejse, hvor jeres far og jeg moedte "Den flyvende handelsmand".
I har sikkert allerede hoert historien om "Den flyvende handelsmand", ikke sandt? "Den flyvende handelsmand" er et spoegelsesskib, der flakker om paa Nordsoeen og Oestersoeen. Dets kaptajn var en graadig handelsmand, der indgik pagt med djaevelen for at oege sin formue. Og han samlede en stor formue, som han skinsygt vogtede paa sit vaeldige skib.
Men en dag kraevede djaevelen sin andel tilbage, og den gnieragtige handelsmand naegtede at betale.
Djaevelen lo ad ham: han skulle nok faa sin haevn. Han forbandede handelsmanden til aldrig at forlade sit skib fuldt af guld og desuden aldrig at finde hvile til tidernes ende. Siden da sejler "Den flyvende handelsmand" paa de nordlige have med sit spoegelsesskib og bringer ulykke over soefolk, der moeder hans skib.
Nok for i dag; som I ser, ryster mine haender blot ved tanken om historien. Lad mig hvile en dag, saa fortaeller jeg resten.

Jakob Blank

column2: Encounter
column3: Moede

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

I promised to tell you the second part of the story today, and I'll keep my word.Your father was a young trader at the time, exactly as you are at the moment. He did not have a lot and captained his snaikka the "Morning Greetings", on which I served as helmsman.
We were on our way with a cargo from Bremen, when a sail appeared on the horizon and quickly came nearer. We quickly realised what was coming towards us, then the "Morning Greetings" had just sailed into a calm. It could only be a ghost ship, and it was flying across the waves at full sail. Everyone at that time knew the story of the "flying trader", and as the ghost ship's dinghy rowed towards us, we hid ourselves behind some barrels.
As a ghostlike shape stepped on board and loudly shouted for the captain of the ship, your father and I sprang into the dinghy and fled as quickly as we could row.We made inquires about "Morning Greetings" at the next port, but it was nowhere to be seen. There was still no news of it in the weeks that followed, so we reported it as sunk in the storm, and cashed in on the insurance. 
However, your father and I had let it down, although we were the most experienced sailors on board. We never got rid of this feeling of guilt. 
I can tell from the expression on your face - that you do not believe a single word -, and only believe that, which you can see with your own eyes.
I could give you a chart showing the exact position of the "flying trader", but I do not want have anymore dead sailors on my conscience.
You'll have to form an armed fleet: If you have a ship, which you can use as an Orlogship, then I will show you the location. If you then sailed to your grave in such a fleet, it wouldn't be my fault.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg lovede at fortaelle historiens anden del i dag, og jeg holder mit ord. Jeres far var dengang en ung handelsmand, ligesom I er nu. Han ejede ikke meget og foerte sin snekke "Morgenhilsen", hvor jeg tjente som styrmand.
Vi var paa vej med en last fra Bremen, da et sejl dukkede op i horisonten og hurtigt kom naermere. Vi forstod snart, hvad der naermede sig, for "Morgenhilsen" var netop gaaet i stille. Det kunne kun vaere et spoegelsesskib, og det floej hen over boelgerne for fulde sejl. Alle kendte dengang historien om "Den flyvende handelsmand", og da spoegelsesskibets jolle roede hen imod os, gemte vi os bag nogle toender.
Da en spoegelsesagtig skikkelse steg om bord og hoejlydt raabte paa skibets kaptajn, sprang jeres far og jeg i jollen og flygtede saa hurtigt, vi kunne ro. I naeste havn spurgte vi efter "Morgenhilsen", men den var ingen steder at se. Heller ikke i ugerne derefter kom der nyt, saa vi meldte den forlist i stormen og haevede forsikringen.
Alligevel havde jeres far og jeg svigtet den, skoent vi var de mest erfarne soefolk om bord. Den skyldfoelelse blev vi aldrig af med.
Jeg ser paa jeres ansigt, at I ikke tror et ord og kun tror paa det, I ser med egne oejne.
Jeg kunne give jer et soekort med den noejagtige position af "Den flyvende handelsmand", men jeg vil ikke have flere doede soefolk paa samvittigheden.
I maa danne en bevaebnet flaade: har I et skib, som I kan bruge som orlogsskib, saa viser jeg jer stedet. Sejler I saa med saadan en flaade mod jeres grav, er det ikke min skyld.

Jakob Blank

column2: Destruction
column3: Fordaerv

column2:
Fool that I am, that's what I get for challenging fate. Everyone knows, that if you have escaped from the "flying trader" you are not allowed to relate the story, never!  And I, the unbeliever, even offered to disclose its whereabouts.
Ever since my garrulous stupidity, the once rich Stetin has been plagued by epidemics and crop failures. Pirates lay in wait on every ship that wants to supply the town with the most needed necessities. 
I have brought a great disaster over the only place in this world that still means something to me. Stetin once had a population of over 3500 inhabitants but soon; you won't be able to find it on any map.
Coming generations will remember: Stetin; the lost town, the town that had to perish because of the stupidity of a single person. Oh wretched me! I cannot tell you where the "flying trader" is. It would cause a great misfortune come about.
Go away and come back only when my hometown has been saved!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Taabe som jeg er, saadan gaar det, naar man udfordrer skaebnen. Alle ved, at den, der er undsluppet "Den flyvende handelsmand", aldrig maa fortaelle historien, aldrig! Og jeg, den vantro, tilboed endda at roebe, hvor han er.
Siden min snakkesalige dumhed hjemsoeges det engang saa rige Stettin af farsoter og misvaekst. Pirater ligger paa lur efter hvert skib, der vil forsyne byen med det allermest noedvendige.
Jeg har bragt en stor ulykke over det eneste sted i verden, der stadig betyder noget for mig. Stettin havde engang over 3500 indbyggere, men snart vil I ikke finde den paa noget kort.
Kommende slaegter vil huske: Stettin, den fortabte by, byen der maatte gaa under paa grund af et enkelt menneskes dumhed. Ve mig! Jeg kan ikke sige jer, hvor "Den flyvende handelsmand" er. Det ville bringe stor ulykke.
Gaa jeres vej, og kom foerst igen, naar min hjemby er reddet!

Jakob Blank

column2: Sad person
column3: Soergelig skikkelse

column2:
Brave Leopold!

You have taken it upon yourself to save this town; condemned to doom? Indeed, the citizens of Stetin deserve nothing less than this, grant asylum to this poor sinner Blank.  He was driven out of Riga in shame and disgrace, which wasn't funny. Stetin opened its door to him because he paid a generous donation into the town treasury, which the fat councillors then put into their own pockets.
Stetin's fatty days are over, and believe me; you can't bring them back even if you tried!

H. Vanderdeeken
column3:
Tapre Leopold!

I har paataget jer at redde denne by, doemt til undergang? Sandelig fortjener Stettins borgere intet mindre, de som gav ly til denne stakkels synder Blank. Han blev jaget ud af Riga med skam og vanaere, og det var ikke til at grine ad. Stettin aabnede sine porte for ham, fordi han betalte en gavmild gave til byens kasse, som de fede raadmaend siden stak i egne lommer.
Stettins fede aar er forbi, og tro mig: I faar dem ikke tilbage, selv om I proever!

H. Vanderdeeken

column2: Rescue
column3: Redning

column2:
Noble Jantzen!

Saviour of Stetin, you have shown truly great courage in standing by my hometown against the raging storms of fate. Your success has strengthened my decision to tell you my last secret: The position, where you are most likely to meet the  "flying trader" is.

Be careful, and God be with you!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Aedle Jantzen!

Stettins redningsmand, I har vist sandt stort mod ved at staa min hjemby bi mod skaebnens rasende storme. Jeres succes har styrket min beslutning om at fortaelle jer min sidste hemmelighed: den position, hvor I med stoerst sandsynlighed moeder "Den flyvende handelsmand".

Vaer forsigtig, og Gud vaere med jer!

Jakob Blank

column2: Musty hulk
column3: Muggen holk

column2:
Dear Sir!

We went to the position marked on the chart and waited there. The wind suddenly became calm and we slowly rode the current. A second ship with ragged sails was being carried by strong currents diagonally towards us. As soon as a light breeze set in, we boarded the ship and examined it carefully.It was just a dilapidated old hulk; in its cargo rooms there were stacks of empty decayed trunks and caskets.
There wasn't a crew on board, nor were there any signs that it had recently been used. We sank the ship according to your orders, and this is my full report.

With nautical greetings,

Captain of the {%s:09}
column3:
Herre!

Vi sejlede til den position, der var afmaerket paa kortet, og ventede der. Pludselig lagde vinden sig, og vi drev langsomt med stroemmen. Et andet skib med laset sejl blev af staerke stroemme foert skraat hen imod os. Saa snart en let brise satte ind, entrede vi skibet og undersoegte det noeje. Det var blot en forfalden gammel holk; i lastrummene stod stabler af tomme, raadne kister og skrin.
Der var ingen besaetning om bord og ingen tegn paa, at skibet for nylig var blevet brugt. Vi saenkede skibet efter jeres ordre, og dette er min fulde rapport.

Med soemandshilsen,

Kaptajnen paa {%s:09}

column2: Relief
column3: Lettelse

column2:
Brave Jantzen!

I have heard about your meeting with the ghost ship. Because you and your entire crew got away, it would appear that the curse of the "travelling trader" has now at last been broken.  Christian shipping is greatly indebted to you, much more than that however, is that I owe you a great debt of gratitude, then you have removed a dark shadow from my soul.There is a rumour that you would now like to be elected Lord Mayor of Bremen, and put this complacent Vanderdeeken in his place. I would love to be in on it, but freed from this terrible burden, I will now peacefully enter the kingdom of the dead. 

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
Tapre Jantzen!

Jeg har hoert om jeres moede med spoegelsesskibet. Da I og hele jeres besaetning slap derfra, synes forbandelsen over "Den flyvende handelsmand" endelig at vaere brudt. Den kristne skibsfart staar i stor gaeld til jer, men endnu mere skylder jeg jer stor tak, for I har fjernet en moerk skygge fra min sjael. Rygtet siger, at I nu vil vaelges til borgmester i Bremen og saette den selvglade Vanderdeeken paa plads. Hvor gerne ville jeg vaere med, men befriet fra denne forfaerdelige byrde gaar jeg nu i fred ind i de doedes rige.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2:
Estate of the late Mr Jakob Blank

Mr Jakob Blank died of natural causes at his home in Stetin last night. He leaves no dependents and his recently modified Last Will and Testament declares {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen as sole benefactor.An examination of his estate shows that Mr Blank who lived in poor conditions had change to the amount of 500.000\C.
The full amount will be transferred to you immediately.

Finance Officer, Stetin
{%+:0C}
column3:
Bo efter afdoede hr. Jakob Blank

Hr. Jakob Blank doede i nat en naturlig doed i sit hjem i Stettin. Han efterlader ingen paaroerende, og hans nyligt aendrede testamente indsaetter {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen som eneste arving. En gennemgang af boet viser, at hr. Blank, der levede under fattige kaar, ejede summen af 500.000\C.
Hele beloebet overfoeres straks til jer.

Byens kaemner i Stettin
{%+:0C}

column2: Move
column3: Flytning

column2:
Young Sir!

I congratulate you on your latest deeds. The house has been in euphoric mood since the arrival of your latest news. Everyone is busy making last minute preparations for the move to Bremen.
Your plan is the talk of the entire Hanse; there has even been a message from a cousin from Novgorod wishing you good luck.
Indeed, the citizens of Lubeck regret loosing their most prominent Councilor, but everyone hopes that you'll teach the unpopular Vanderdeeken a lesson.

Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Jeg lykoensker jer med jeres seneste bedrifter. Huset har vaeret i den hoejeste begejstring, siden jeres seneste nyheder kom. Alle har travlt med de sidste forberedelser til flytningen til Bremen.
Jeres plan er paa alles laeber i hele Hansaen; der er endda kommet et budskab fra en faetter i Novgorod, der oensker jer held og lykke.
Ganske vist beklager Luebecks borgere at miste deres fornemste raadmand, men alle haaber, at I vil give den upopulaere Vanderdeeken en laerestreg.

Jeres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Warning
column3: Advarsel

column2:
Now, Master Jantzen!

Have you come to Bremen to offer me your services? Oh no, I hear you wanted to become Lord Mayor in my town. The rabble and its kind are supporting you in this foolish undertaking, as well, what!
I'll say this as a warning: the people, who are now cheering for you, are only driven by their own jealousies. They are jealous of my wealth and my power, but if the truth were known, they admire, and are afraid of me.
They would never speak out publicly against me, and I'll give you this well-meant advice, do the same.
Only because you can sink an old decaying ship, doesn't, in my eyes make you anything more than a "good for nothing", who was brought up in an arrogant way by his father.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Naa, mester Jantzen!

Er I kommet til Bremen for at tilbyde mig jeres tjenester? Aah nej, jeg hoerer, at I ville vaere borgmester i min by. Poebelen og dens lige stoetter jer i dette taabelige forehavende, sandelig!
Jeg siger dette som en advarsel: de, der nu hylder jer, drives kun af deres egen misundelse. De misunder min rigdom og min magt, men i virkeligheden beundrer og frygter de mig.
Aldrig ville de offentligt tale imod mig, og jeg giver jer det velmente raad at goere det samme.
Blot fordi I kan saenke et gammelt raaddent skib, er I i mine oejne intet andet end en "doegenigt", opdraget i hovmod af sin far.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Sincerity
column3: Oprigtighed

column2:
Colleague Jantzen,

I am seriously worried about your father's soul. Your father had to pawn his entire future wealth to progress half as much again in his career, and I really wouldn't want to know what sort of crooked business would bring you so quickly forward. 
I hardly believe that the sudden wealth, which you so uninhibitedly display to the public, is earned by honest work. Are you not making the same mistake as once did your father?

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Kollega Jantzen,

Jeg er alvorligt bekymret for jeres fars sjael. Jeres far maatte pantsaette hele sin fremtidige formue for at komme halvt saa langt i sin loebebane, og jeg vil virkelig ikke vide, hvilke lyssky forretninger der bringer jer saa hurtigt frem.
Jeg tror naeppe, at den pludselige rigdom, som I saa ugenert fremviser offentligt, er tjent ved aerligt arbejde. Begaar I ikke den samme fejl som engang jeres far?

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
Damn you Jantzen!

That you always have to get involved in things, which you do not wish to understand. Obviously, you have a certain talent for manipulating people and have robbed me of making a beautiful speech, Dear Lord Mayor.
But it doesn't matter, there are enumerable others.
You may now be laughing maliciously and in triumph but I'll get my own back. Sooner or later, we'll meet again, I can already promise you that.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Forbandede Jantzen!

At I altid skal blande jer i ting, som I ikke vil forstaa. Oejensynlig har I et vist talent for at styre folk og har beroevet mig en smuk tale, kaere borgmester.
Men lige meget, der er utallige andre.
I ler maaske nu skadefro og triumferende, men jeg skal faa min haevn. Foer eller siden moedes vi igen, det kan jeg allerede love jer.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
Dear Lord Mayor Jantzen!

A letter arrived here sometime ago from Stetin; it was addressed to " Lord Mayor Jantzen of Bremen". We assumed it was a mistake and sent it back. But it was sent again from Stetin and then it became forgotten, until I, on the occasion of your taking over office as Lord Mayor, remembered it. It appears that letter must have been addressed to you and that we may deliver it, now that you are lord Mayor.

The Post Office Bremen.
column3:
Kaere borgmester Jantzen!

For nogen tid siden kom der et brev hertil fra Stettin; det var adresseret til "borgmester Jantzen i Bremen". Vi troede, det var en fejl, og sendte det tilbage. Men det blev sendt igen fra Stettin og gik derefter i glemmebogen, indtil jeg huskede det i anledning af jeres tiltraedelse som borgmester. Det lader til, at brevet var stilet til jer, og at vi maa aflevere det, nu hvor I er borgmester.

Posthuset i Bremen.

column2: Dept
column3: Gaeld

column2:
\f1_Here the letter kept for you.
\f3_

\rStetin, {%D:11}
\lI poor sinner!

A little while ago, one of your sailors came to the bed in which I will die shortly. He was on the trip to the ghost ship and should now relate the events in every single detail to me. From his story, and to my horror, I realised that you were not personally there.
This naturally changes every thing; then with your father's money in your pocket you would have to have seen the ghost ship. I am taking on double and triple burden of guilt on myself, to warn you with this letter, at least, of the imminent disaster.

At our last meeting you mentioned that you were the Lord Mayor of Bremen. That must be the quickest way for this letter reach you, and then you at least, can save your soul. However one thing at a time:
I did not tell you the whole truth about the "flying trader" and my meeting with the ghost ship.

Namely, if he who is of a pure conscience and without ambitions of profit, meets the ghost ship, he will see nothing more in it than a over a hundred year old weather beaten ship and is at first, not in any danger.
However, he who goes on board with greed in his heart, or has part of the treasure of the ghost ship in his moneybag, will be met by an appearance of the greedy trader and a deal suggested. He, who agrees, gets a share of the treasure but sells the souls of all honourable seamen on board for it.
The treasure is enchanted and multiplies itself almost automatically, the curse however, is this; to strive to get back to its master and in the end brings nothing but misfortune for the illegal owner.

Your father's business was not doing well at the time and he had fallen in love with a beautiful girl in Lubeck, whose father did want anything to do with a poor man's wedding. I had lost a lot of money gambling, and so we were sitting a tavern in Bremen, thinking about what to do before this unfortunate journey, when a stranger came to our table. He knew all about our situation and offered us his support. What he demanded for it was nothing less than a fair share of our future wealth. We agreed because we didn't have anything to lose, and he said that; on our next journey a ship with which we could make the deal of our lives would meet us.
I do not need to describe the details of coming events, I'm sure you can already guess them. We sold "Morning Greetings" to the "flying trader" and landed ashore with a dinghy full of gold.
From now on we seem to have nothing but luck, your father got his girl and quickly climbed the career ladder in Lubeck. I paid off my debts and above that won large sums until one day the stranger turned up again. At first, he demanded your father's sweet little baby daughter. Then he came to me: I refused to pay the price he demanded from me and was driven as a common criminal from my then hometown. Since then I have been, once or twice, on the run and lost contact with your father as a result. It was only in Stetin that I more or less returned to a normal life, but I never touched any of the money, which I still had. And now I'll have to die with sins because I never told you the whole truth in time. I can only advice you to hide all your father's money and that which I will leave you for safekeeping. Do not touch it, under no circumstances should use it as an investment, otherwise the curse of the  "flying trader" will be on you, and you'll never find peace in this world.

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
\f1_Her er brevet, der blev gemt til jer.
\f3_

\rStettin, {%D:11}
\lJeg arme synder!

For kort tid siden kom en af jeres matroser hen til den seng, hvor jeg snart skal doe. Han var med paa rejsen til spoegelsesskibet og skulle nu fortaelle mig begivenhederne i alle enkeltheder. Af hans beretning forstod jeg til min raedsel, at I ikke selv var med.
Det aendrer naturligvis alt, for med jeres fars penge i lommen skulle I ellers have set spoegelsesskibet. Jeg paatager mig dobbelt og tredobbelt skyld og vil med dette brev i det mindste advare jer mod den forestaaende ulykke.

Ved vort sidste moede naevnte I, at I er borgmester i Bremen. Der maa dette brev naa jer hurtigst, og saa kan i det mindste I redde jeres sjael. Men én ting ad gangen:
Jeg fortalte ikke hele sandheden om "Den flyvende handelsmand" og mit moede med spoegelsesskibet.

Den, der nemlig med ren samvittighed og uden vindesyge moeder spoegelsesskibet, ser intet andet i det end et skib, der er vejrbidt gennem aarhundreder, og er til at begynde med ikke i fare.
Men den, der gaar om bord med graadighed i hjertet, eller baerer en del af spoegelsesskibets skat i sin pung, moeder et syn af den graadige handelsmand, som foreslaar en handel. Den, der slaar til, faar en del af skatten, men saelger til gengaeld sjaelene af alle haederlige soefolk om bord.
Skatten er forhekset og formerer sig naesten af sig selv, men dens forbandelse er at straebe tilbage til sin herre og til sidst intet bringe den uretmaessige ejer end ulykke.

Jeres fars forretninger gik ikke godt dengang, og han havde forelsket sig i en smuk pige i Luebeck, hvis far ikke ville vide af et fattigt bryllup. Jeg havde tabt mange penge ved spil, og saa sad vi foer denne ulykkelige rejse og raadslog paa en kro i Bremen, da en fremmed traadte hen til vort bord. Han vidste alt om vor noed og tilboed sin stoette. Hvad han forlangte for den, var intet andet end en rimelig andel af vor fremtidige rigdom. Vi slog til, da vi intet havde at tabe, og han sagde, at vi paa vor naeste rejse ville moede et skib, med hvilket vi kunne goere vort livs handel.
Jeg behoever ikke beskrive enkelthederne i det, der fulgte; I gaetter dem sikkert allerede. Vi solgte "Morgenhilsen" til "Den flyvende handelsmand" og naaede fastlandet med en jolle fuld af guld.
Fra da af syntes lykken at smile til os: jeres far fik sin pige og gjorde hurtigt karriere i Luebeck. Jeg betalte min gaeld og vandt oven i koebet store summer, indtil den fremmede en dag dukkede op igen. Foerst kraevede han jeres fars soede lille datter. Siden kom han til mig: jeg naegtede at betale den pris, han kraevede, og blev jaget ud af min davaerende hjemby som en simpel forbryder. Siden har jeg gang paa gang vaeret paa flugt og mistede derved kontakten til jeres far. Foerst i Stettin fandt jeg igen et nogenlunde normalt liv, men de penge, jeg havde tilbage, roerte jeg aldrig. Og nu maa jeg doe med synder, fordi jeg ikke i tide fortalte jer hele sandheden. Jeg kan kun raade jer til at skjule alle jeres fars penge og det, jeg efterlader jer til opbevaring. Roer dem ikke, og brug dem under ingen omstaendigheder til at formere dem, ellers rammer "Den flyvende handelsmands" forbandelse jer, og I vil aldrig finde fred i denne verden.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank
