column3: Opgavens maal

column2:
You now have a year to rise from shopkeeper to trader.

Luebeck's strengths lie in fishing and the production of iron goods. Wood and bricks are also produced there, so you shouldn't have any problems constructing new buildings.

On the other hand, Luebeck only produces a little grain and no beer at all. So first of all, you should concentrate on getting beer from Stettin or Gdansk. You can also go to Hamburg or Bremen, but they are both further away.

Gdansk is always short of iron goods and sometimes of fish too. Stettin also urgently needs iron goods.

Make sure that you don't pay too much for the goods. The limits are around 450\C for fish, 450\C for iron goods and 50\C for beer.
column3:
I har nu ét aar til at avancere fra kraemmer til handelsmand.

Luebecks styrke ligger i fiskeriet og fremstillingen af jernvarer. Der fremstilles ogsaa trae og mursten, saa I burde ikke faa problemer med at opfoere nye bygninger.

Til gengaeld fremstiller Luebeck kun lidt korn og slet ingen oel. Koncentrer jer derfor foerst om at skaffe oel fra Stettin eller Gdansk. I kan ogsaa sejle til Hamburg eller Bremen, men de ligger begge laengere vaek.

Gdansk mangler altid jernvarer og af og til ogsaa fisk. Ogsaa Stettin har haardt brug for jernvarer.

Soerg for ikke at betale for meget for varerne. Graenserne ligger omkring 450\C for fisk, 450\C for jernvarer og 50\C for oel.

column2:
Because trade in iron goods is important, you should ensure that there is always enough pig iron in Luebeck, as this raw material cannot be produced here.
This is however produced in Oslo, for instance. This town is also an appreciative buyer of grain, iron goods and beer.

However, you should always sell as many goods to Luebeck as possible, as this is the quickest way to increase your recognition, so that your advancement to trader status will not take too long.

Incidentally, don't start producing any buildings or ships yet. We can come back to that once you have achieved trader status.
column3:
Da handlen med jernvarer er vigtig, boer I soerge for, at der altid er nok raajern i Luebeck, for dette raastof kan ikke fremstilles her.
Det fremstilles derimod for eksempel i Oslo. Den by koeber ogsaa gerne korn, jernvarer og oel.

Saelg dog altid saa mange varer som muligt til Luebeck, for det er den hurtigste maade at oege jeres anseelse paa, saa jeres forfremmelse til handelsmand ikke tager for lang tid.

Begynd i oevrigt ikke at bygge bygninger eller skibe endnu. Det vender vi tilbage til, naar I er blevet handelsmand.

column2:
Now you must make it from trader to merchant status. You have 6 months to do this. Besides trading, you should now build facilities and town houses in your home town.

As you know, Luebeck's strengths are fishing and the manufacture of iron goods. Start by building a facility for each of these industries. You may have to get the raw building materials for these from other towns. But you should only construct one of each building to start with, as you will also have to find buyers for your goods.

Building facilities brings you two advantages besides trade: firstly, your reputation grows with every worker that you employ. Secondly, creating new workplaces draws new citizens into the town. This increases demand and you can sell more goods.

If your facilities are to fill up with workers quickly, the poor townspeople must at the very least be contented. You should therefore continue to take good care of the town. The workers also need somewhere to live. If existing town houses are too overcrowded, you should build a new one.
column3:
Nu skal I avancere fra handelsmand til koebmand. I har 6 maaneder til det. Ud over handlen boer I nu bygge vaerksteder og borgerhuse i jeres hjemby.

Som I ved, ligger Luebecks styrke i fiskeriet og fremstillingen af jernvarer. Begynd med at bygge et vaerksted for hvert af disse erhverv. Maaske maa I hente byggematerialerne fra andre byer. Men byg til at begynde med kun én bygning af hver slags, for I skal ogsaa finde koebere til jeres varer.

Vaerksteder giver jer to fordele ud over handlen: for det foerste vokser jeres ry med hver arbejder, I ansaetter. For det andet traekker nye arbejdspladser nye borgere til byen. Det oeger efterspoergslen, og I kan saelge flere varer.

Skal jeres vaerksteder hurtigt fyldes med arbejdere, maa byens fattige i det mindste vaere tilfredse. Bliv derfor ved med at soerge godt for byen. Arbejderne har ogsaa brug for et sted at bo. Er de eksisterende huse overfyldte, boer I bygge et nyt.

column2:
Bear in mind that your facilities need raw materials. These must be available from your trading office.

If you have a trading office manager, he can buy in the raw materials when the town needs them. You don't need to worry about this at the moment though, especially since a manager also costs money.

To see which raw materials your facilities need, click on a facility once it is completed. You can also find out from your trading office what all of your facilities in the town need.
column3:
Husk, at jeres vaerksteder har brug for raavarer. De skal vaere til raadighed i jeres kontor.

Har I en kontorforvalter, kan han koebe raavarerne ind, naar byen har brug for dem. Det behoever I dog ikke bekymre jer om lige nu, isaer da en forvalter ogsaa koster penge.

For at se, hvilke raavarer jeres vaerksteder har brug for, klikker I paa et vaerksted, naar det er faerdigt. I jeres kontor kan I ogsaa se, hvad alle jeres vaerksteder i byen har brug for.

column2:
To become a merchant, you naturally need to acquire even greater recognition and amass considerable wealth. You should concentrate on cloth, wine and meat for the richer inhabitants of your home town. Try adding furs too - you will find them in the east.

If you should ever happen to come across spices, buy them! They are another much sought-after product with the rich citizens of Luebeck.
column3:
For at blive koebmand behoever I naturligvis endnu stoerre anseelse og en betydelig formue. Koncentrer jer om klaede, vin og koed til de rigere indbyggere i jeres hjemby. Proev ogsaa med skind - dem finder I mod oest.

Skulle I nogensinde stoede paa krydderier, saa koeb dem! De er en anden meget eftertragtet vare hos Luebecks rige borgere.

column2:
To transport the manufactured goods out of the town more efficiently, you should own at least one more ship. Commission a snaikka or crayer from the Luebeck shipyard.

Use your Luebeck shipyard as often as possible - including for repairs - because the more orders it gets, the better the ships will be that are built there.
column3:
For mere effektivt at fragte de fremstillede varer ud af byen boer I eje mindst ét skib mere. Bestil en snekke eller en kraier hos vaerftet i Luebeck.

Brug jeres vaerft i Luebeck saa ofte som muligt - ogsaa til reparationer - for jo flere ordrer det faar, desto bedre bliver de skibe, der bygges der.

column2: All you need to advance from merchant to long distance merchant is a bit more recognition and some extra wealth. You must also be a member of the guild - which is sure to increase your reputation.\nOnce again, you have 6 months to complete your rise in status.\n
column3: Alt, hvad I behoever for at avancere fra koebmand til fjernhandelsmand, er lidt mere anseelse og lidt ekstra formue. I skal ogsaa vaere medlem af lavet - hvilket sikkert vil oege jeres ry.\nIgen har I 6 maaneder til forfremmelsen.\n

column2:
Bear in mind that your wealth includes not only your cash, but also facilities, town houses, ships and stored goods. However, any debts that you have with the moneylender are deducted.

If living space becomes limited in Luebeck, you should quickly build an appropriate number of town houses, as every tenant will bring you - just like every worker that you employ - additional recognition amongst the tenants. If you are too slow, your competitors, or the town itself may build town houses, in which case you will find it harder to fill your own. As the town houses also cost you weekly land taxes, they must be adequately populated to ensure that you can make a profit. The utilisation rate for half-timbered houses must therefore be over 70{%%:00}, while the utilisation rate for other houses must be at least 50{%%:00}.
column3:
Husk, at jeres formue ikke kun omfatter rede penge, men ogsaa vaerksteder, borgerhuse, skibe og oplagrede varer. Gaeld hos laangiveren traekkes dog fra.

Bliver boligpladsen knap i Luebeck, boer I hurtigt bygge et passende antal borgerhuse, for hver lejer giver jer - ligesom hver arbejder, I ansaetter - ekstra anseelse blandt lejerne. Er I for langsomme, kan jeres konkurrenter eller byen selv bygge borgerhuse, og saa bliver det svaerere at fylde jeres egne. Da borgerhusene ogsaa koster jer ugentlig grundskat, skal de vaere tilstraekkeligt beboede, for at I kan tjene penge. Belaegningen i bindingsvaerkshuse skal derfor vaere over 70{%%:00}, i andre huse mindst 50{%%:00}.

column2: Have you joined the Luebeck Guild yet? You must be a member of a guild before you can attain the status of long distance merchant or higher.\nBy the way, the guild entry fee increases as you become wealthier. It also decreases as your reputation in the town grows.\n
column3: Er I allerede traadt ind i lavet i Luebeck? I skal vaere medlem af et lav, foer I kan naa fjernhandelsmands rang eller hoejere.\nI oevrigt stiger lavets indskud, jo rigere I bliver. Det falder ogsaa, efterhaanden som jeres ry i byen vokser.\n

column2:
You must acquire a considerable increase in reputation with all the town's inhabitants within a year, if you are to advance to councillor status. As you also need to be much wealthier, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown, as investments increase your wealth and enhance your reputation.
Double or treble your production in Luebeck and build town houses in plenty of time, so that the new workers and their families can become your tenants. 
As your production increases, you also need to build new ships, so that the goods being produced can be transported.
column3:
I skal inden for et aar oege jeres ry betydeligt blandt alle byens indbyggere for at blive raadmand. Da I ogsaa skal vaere meget rigere, boer I investere saa meget som muligt i jeres hjemby, for investeringer oeger jeres formue og hoejner jeres ry.
Fordobl eller tredobl jeres produktion i Luebeck, og byg borgerhuse i god tid, saa de nye arbejdere og deres familier kan blive jeres lejere.
Efterhaanden som jeres produktion stiger, faar I ogsaa brug for nye skibe, saa de fremstillede varer kan fragtes.

column2:
Here are a couple more hints that may help you to improve your reputation.
Basically, all you need to know is that everything you do for your home town means a better reputation. If you spend money on the church or the public bath, your reputation increases. If you issue a loan or construct buildings and facilities, it increases again. It can also benefit from family, organisation of a celebration, a large fortune or the provision of guard ships. 
But it can also deteriorate if, for example, a criminal offence comes to light, if you demolish facilities or if you demand a high interest rate when extending a loan.
Incidentally, your recognition can also increase following a successful expedition, as all Hansa towns benefit from this. Just undertake an expedition every now and again, and discover new places to sell your wares.
column3:
Her er et par raad mere, som kan hjaelpe jer med at forbedre jeres ry.
Grundlaeggende behoever I kun at vide, at alt, hvad I goer for jeres hjemby, betyder bedre ry. Bruger I penge paa kirken eller det offentlige bad, stiger jeres ry. Yder I et laan eller bygger bygninger og vaerksteder, stiger det igen. Ogsaa familien, at holde en fest, en stor formue eller at stille vagtskibe til raadighed gavner det.
Men det kan ogsaa forringes, hvis for eksempel en forbrydelse kommer for dagen, hvis I river vaerksteder ned, eller hvis I kraever hoej rente, naar I yder et laan.
Jeres anseelse kan i oevrigt ogsaa vokse efter en vellykket ekspedition, for alle hansestaeder nyder godt af den. Foretag altsaa en ekspedition en gang imellem, og opdag nye steder at afsaette jeres varer.

column2:
To enable you to gain even more profit from trade, you should build a trading office in as many other towns as possible and produce goods there. It isn't always cheaper to produce goods yourself than to buy them at a low price. But by producing goods yourself, you can be sure of a constant price and a consistent quantity. This is particularly useful for setting up trade routes, to ensure a continuous supply to your home town, for example, or to exchange your own goods between two or more trading offices.
But be careful how you select your facilities. Think about which goods the towns are still likely to need in the future. Because if you produce more than can be used, the goods will stock pile in the towns and the price (and therefore your profit) will decrease in the long run.
column3:
For at faa endnu mere ud af handlen boer I bygge et kontor i saa mange andre byer som muligt og fremstille varer der. Det er ikke altid billigere at fremstille selv end at koebe billigt. Men ved at fremstille selv er I sikre paa en fast pris og en jaevn maengde. Det er saerlig nyttigt, naar I opretter handelsruter, for eksempel for stadig at forsyne jeres hjemby eller udveksle jeres egne varer mellem to eller flere kontorer.
Men vaer omhyggelige med valget af vaerksteder. Taenk over, hvilke varer byerne sandsynligvis stadig faar brug for i fremtiden. For fremstiller I mere, end der kan bruges, hober varerne sig op i byerne, og prisen (og dermed jeres fortjeneste) falder i det lange loeb.

column2:
To enable you to gain even more profit from trade, you should build a trading office in as many other towns as possible and produce goods there. It isn't always cheaper to produce goods yourself than to buy them at a low price. But by producing goods yourself, you can be sure of a constant price and a consistent quantity. This is particularly useful for setting up trade routes, to ensure a continuous supply to your home town, for example, or to exchange your own goods between two or more trading offices.
But be careful how you select your facilities. Think about which goods the towns are still likely to need in the future. Because if you produce more than can be used, the goods will mount up in the towns and the price (and therefore your profit) will decrease over time. 
If particular goods that you are producing are no longer profitable, don't hesitate about shutting them down or demolishing the relevant facility.
column3:
For at faa endnu mere ud af handlen boer I bygge et kontor i saa mange andre byer som muligt og fremstille varer der. Det er ikke altid billigere at fremstille selv end at koebe billigt. Men ved at fremstille selv er I sikre paa en fast pris og en jaevn maengde. Det er saerlig nyttigt, naar I opretter handelsruter, for eksempel for stadig at forsyne jeres hjemby eller udveksle jeres egne varer mellem to eller flere kontorer.
Men vaer omhyggelige med valget af vaerksteder. Taenk over, hvilke varer byerne sandsynligvis stadig faar brug for i fremtiden. For fremstiller I mere, end der kan bruges, hober varerne sig op i byerne, og prisen (og dermed jeres fortjeneste) falder med tiden.
Er visse varer, som I fremstiller, ikke laengere rentable, saa toev ikke med at standse produktionen eller rive det paagaeldende vaerksted ned.

column2: The main thing you need to focus on is achieving popularity in your home town, even when rising to the rank of Patrician. Only when you have achieved this step will you be able to aim for the position of Lord Mayor.
column3: Det vigtigste er, at I vinder popularitet i jeres hjemby, ogsaa for at naa patriciers rang. Foerst naar I har taget det skridt, kan I straebe efter borgmesterembedet.

column2:
You're on the right track!
But if you want to become a trader, you will also have to look after the rich citizens in Luebeck. These folk aren't that bothered about beer and grain so you should try to make them happier with meat, wine and cloth.
 
You can get meat in Aalborg and Bergen. But make sure that Aalborg has enough salt, otherwise no meat can be produced there. You can take some salt with you from Luebeck.

You can get wine from Cologne. The citizens there could do with some fish and beer.

There is plenty of cloth available in Visby. Find out what they need there.
column3:
I er paa rette vej!
Men vil I vaere handelsmand, maa I ogsaa tage jer af de rige borgere i Luebeck. Det folk bryder sig ikke meget om oel og korn, saa proev at goere dem gladere med koed, vin og klaede.
 
Koed faar I i Aalborg og Bergen. Men soerg for, at Aalborg har salt nok, ellers kan der ikke fremstilles koed der. I kan tage lidt salt med fra Luebeck.

Vin faar I fra Cologne. Borgerne der kunne godt bruge lidt fisk og oel.

I Visby er der klaede i overflod. Find ud af, hvad man har brug for der.

column2:
Normally, your reputation in a town increases whenever you supply goods to the town. However, this only applies if the town actually needs that particular product. You can tell if a product is no longer required when the sales price is very close to the purchase price. 

Incidentally, you can also lose reputation in a town by buying up scarce goods. So don't do this in your home town!
column3:
Normalt vokser jeres ry i en by, hver gang I leverer varer dertil. Det gaelder dog kun, hvis byen virkelig har brug for netop den vare. I kan se, at en vare ikke laengere behoeves, naar salgsprisen ligger meget taet paa indkoebsprisen.

I kan i oevrigt ogsaa miste anseelse i en by ved at opkoebe knappe varer. Goer det altsaa ikke i jeres hjemby!

column2: You will notice little product icons against the different towns on the sea map. These indicate which goods are most urgently required.\nBe careful: this information takes a while to reach you, so an icon may already be out of date by the time you arrive in the town. If you want to use these icons to make extra profit, you must therefore concentrate your efforts on the towns in the area immediately surrounding Luebeck.\n
column3: I vil se smaa varesymboler ved de forskellige byer paa soekortet. De viser, hvilke varer der er mest akut brug for.\nPas paa: disse oplysninger er et stykke tid om at naa jer, saa et symbol kan allerede vaere foraeldet, naar I ankommer til byen. Vil I bruge symbolerne til ekstra fortjeneste, maa I derfor koncentrere jeres indsats om byerne i Luebecks umiddelbare omegn.\n

column2: Bear in mind that your rank is bestowed on you by your home town, so the main thing is therefore that you are well known in this town. Your current rank is displayed in your trading office overview.\n\n
column3: Husk, at jeres rang tildeles jer af jeres hjemby, saa det vigtigste er, at I er velkendt der. Jeres nuvaerende rang vises i oversigten over jeres kontor.\n\n

column2: Winter is drawing near! Buy grain and beer and store it in your trading office, so that you can still provide for your home town in winter and gain a good reputation with the citizens.
column3: Vinteren naermer sig! Koeb korn og oel og oplagr det i jeres kontor, saa I ogsaa om vinteren kan forsyne jeres hjemby og vinde et godt ry blandt borgerne.

column2:
My dearest son,

You are now old enough to follow in my footsteps, but you must gain your own experiences first.

I spent some happy times roaming the entire Hanseatic region as a free trader and captain of a glorious Snaikka, before settling down in {%t:01} to fulfil my political commitments and marry your mother. I would like you to follow in my footsteps and be admitted to the Hanseatic League on your own merits. As start-up capital, You will recieved a Snaikka, a Crayer, and a trading office in {%t:01} - so that we might see each other once in a while - and some cash. This should make it easy for you to achieve the rank of trader.

Your loving father, 

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaereste soen,

Nu er du gammel nok til at foelge i mine fodspor, men foerst maa du goere dine egne erfaringer.

Jeg havde lykkelige tider, hvor jeg drog rundt i hele Hansaens omraade som fri handelsmand og kaptajn paa en praegtig snekke, foer jeg slog mig ned i {%t:01} for at opfylde mine politiske forpligtelser og gifte mig med din mor. Jeg vil gerne, at du foelger i mine fodspor og optages i Hansaen paa egne fortjenester. Som startkapital faar du en snekke, en kraier og et kontor i {%t:01} - saa vi kan ses en gang imellem - samt nogle rede penge. Det burde goere det let for dig at naa handelsmands rang.

Din kaerlige far,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Gone
column3: Borte

column2:
My dearest son,

You have certainly had a splendid education, as you were fortunate enough to be taught by the brightest brains in Europe. But you have barely left dry land so far.
So let me give you some good advice as you go on your way: be as much on your guard against the "Flying Trader" as you would against the Kobold! There are many dangers awaiting you on the open seas, but this ghost ship is the Devil's own spawn.

May God protect you.
P. S. Your mother is worried about you, so please don't be too bold in your youthful recklessness!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaereste soen,

Du har sandelig faaet en glimrende opdragelse, da du var saa heldig at blive undervist af Europas klogeste hoveder. Men indtil nu har du knap nok forladt fast grund.
Lad mig derfor give dig et godt raad med paa vejen: vaer lige saa meget paa vagt over for "Den flyvende handelsmand" som over for nissen! Mange farer venter dig paa det aabne hav, men dette spoegelsesskib er djaevelens eget yngel.

Gud bevare dig.
P.S. Din mor er bekymret for dig, saa vaer ikke for dristig i din ungdommelige dumdristighed!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2:
My dearest son,

I am delighted to see how your business is flourishing. If you carry on like this, you will easily make it to trader and much more besides.

But you mustn't think only of your own financial gain. You should also tend to the needs of the people in the towns you are trading with. Remember: wealth can make you lonely!

However, I have a sad reason for writing to you today. Your mother is ill. She has been confined to bed with a high fever for several days, and even the Hanseatic League's very best doctors have no idea which rare disease she has. I have had a physician from Florence sent for; I only hope he will get here in time!

Love from your mother and me, and take care.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaereste soen,

Det glaeder mig at se, hvor godt dine forretninger blomstrer. Fortsaetter du saadan, bliver du let handelsmand og meget mere.

Men du maa ikke kun taenke paa din egen vinding. Du boer ogsaa tage dig af behovene hos folk i de byer, du handler med. Husk: rigdom kan goere ensom!

Men i dag skriver jeg af en soergelig grund. Din mor er syg. Hun har ligget i sengen med hoej feber i flere dage, og selv Hansaens allerbedste laeger aner ikke, hvilken sjaelden sygdom hun har. Jeg har sendt bud efter en laege fra Firenze; jeg haaber blot, han naar frem i tide!

Kaerlig hilsen fra din mor og mig, og pas paa dig selv.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2:
My dearest son,

Why must joy and sorrow always go together? I had barely shown the mayor out, who had dropped by to tell me about your appointment as trader, when Master Ardovini summoned me. - This is the famous physician that I told you about in my last letter. He arrived in {%t:01} two weeks ago, but even he was unable to treat your mother's mysterious illness.
She died suddenly three days ago, although she had been in a stable condition for a long time and we were beginning to nurture hopes of her recovery. Her body is to be laid to rest in the {%t:01} crypt next Sunday, and I am now starting to feel the ravages of time eating away at me too.

Please be assured of my congratulations on your rapid advancement, in spite of this distressing news!

Your loving father,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaereste soen,

Hvorfor skal glaede og sorg altid foelges ad? Knap havde jeg fulgt borgmesteren ud, der var kommet forbi for at fortaelle om din udnaevnelse til handelsmand, foer mester Ardovini lod mig kalde. - Det er den beroemte laege, jeg skrev om i mit sidste brev. Han kom til {%t:01} for to uger siden, men end ikke han kunne behandle din mors gaadefulde sygdom.
Hun doede pludselig for tre dage siden, skoent hendes tilstand laenge havde vaeret stabil, og vi var begyndt at naere haab om bedring. Hendes legeme skal bisaettes i krypten i {%t:01} paa soendag, og nu begynder ogsaa jeg at maerke tidens tand gnave i mig.

Modtag trods disse triste nyheder min lykoenskning med din hurtige forfremmelse!

Din kaerlige far,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Long Distance Merchant
column3: Fjernhandelsmand

column2:
Dear Leopold,

It is now barely a week since I last wrote to you. I buried your mother yesterday. Now you are all I have left.

May God help my wicked soul, so that I may not lose you as well! You are a cautious trader, and I am sure that you will not disappoint me. I have enclosed 50,000\C with this letter, to help your career advance more quickly.

Once you have achieved the rank of long distance merchant, I wish to entrust you with a secret that has weighed heavy on my mind for many years. Don't ask me about it, as I cannot tell you any more just yet, at least not until I'm sure... No! Away with you, I told him I wouldn't reveal it...


\f1_Young Sir,

Your father has asked me to deliver this letter to you. My mistress's death has hit him so hard that he sometimes seems to be delirious in his waking hours.
However, he already seems to be quite a lot better, so there is no need for you to worry about him.

On behalf of my benevolent master Georg Jantzen,

Your most obedient servant,

\f3_Karl
column3:
Kaere Leopold,

Det er knap en uge siden, jeg sidst skrev til dig. I gaar begravede jeg din mor. Nu er du alt, hvad jeg har tilbage.

Maatte Gud hjaelpe min syndige sjael, saa jeg ikke ogsaa mister dig! Du er en forsigtig handelsmand, og jeg er sikker paa, at du ikke skuffer mig. Jeg har vedlagt 50.000\C til dette brev, saa din loebebane kan gaa hurtigere frem.

Naar du har naaet fjernhandelsmands rang, vil jeg betro dig en hemmelighed, der i mange aar har tynget mit sind. Spoerg mig ikke om den, jeg kan ikke sige mere endnu, i hvert fald ikke foer jeg er sikker... Nej! Vaek med dig, jeg sagde jo til ham, at jeg ikke ville roebe det...


\f1_Unge herre,

Jeres far har bedt mig overbringe jer dette brev. Min frues doed har ramt ham saa haardt, at han af og til synes at tale i vildelse, selv i vaagen tilstand.
Han synes dog allerede at have det en hel del bedre, saa I behoever ikke bekymre jer om ham.

Paa vegne af min velvillige herre Georg Jantzen,

Jeres ydmygeste tjener,

\f3_Karl

column2:
My dearest Son,

I must apologise for my last letter. The worry of the last few weeks weighed heavily on my mind. I am after all, not getting any younger. You, however, have your whole life ahead of you. And although you may not wish to waste any time thinking about this particular subject at the moment, I would like to give you some advice all the same.

I am talking about marriage, and sharing the joys of wedded bliss with a loving bride. My advice is as follows: do look for a kindly, charitable woman, one who is generous to the poor. That will be good for your social reputation and for the salvation of your soul, and even the Kobold will also show you mercy.

May God protect you!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kaereste soen,

Jeg maa undskylde mit sidste brev. De sidste ugers bekymringer tyngede mig svaert. Jeg bliver jo ikke yngre. Du derimod har hele livet foran dig. Og selv om du maaske ikke vil spilde tid paa at taenke paa netop dette emne nu, vil jeg alligevel give dig et raad.

Jeg taler om aegteskabet og om at dele aegtestandens glaeder med en kaerlig brud. Mit raad lyder: soeg en godhjertet, barmhjertig kvinde, som er gavmild mod de fattige. Det vil vaere godt for dit ry og for din sjaels frelse, og selv nissen vil vise dig naade.

Gud bevare dig!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Worries
column3: Bekymringer

column2:
Young sir,

I am very worried about your father. In recent nights, he has been suddenly awakend from terrible dreams with increasing frequency and has been shouting for your dear departed mother and for the priest like a man possessed.
He has had nightmares occasionally before, of course, but never this bad.

He is also refusing to leave the house or to let anybody other than the priest in. He has even decreed that you may only be allowed into the house if you have achieved the title of long distance merchant. In his current state of mind, I would not put it past him to throw you out of the house if you did not have this title.

I am writing you this letter without his knowledge and beg you, if you are able to satisfy his wishes, to come and see your father soon.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Jeg er meget bekymret for jeres far. De seneste naetter er han stadig oftere pludselig blevet vaekket af forfaerdelige droemme og har raabt som en besat paa jeres kaere afdoede mor og paa praesten.
Selvfoelgelig har han af og til haft mareridt foer, men aldrig saa slemme.

Han naegter ogsaa at forlade huset eller lukke andre end praesten ind. Han har endog bestemt, at I kun maa lukkes ind, hvis I har opnaaet titlen fjernhandelsmand. I hans nuvaerende sindstilstand ville det ikke undre mig, om han smed jer ud, hvis I ikke havde denne titel.

Jeg skriver dette brev uden hans vidende og beder jer om, hvis I kan opfylde hans oenske, snart at komme til jeres far.

Jeres ydmygeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Father's Death
column3: Faderens doed

column2:
Young Sir,

It is my sad duty to report a tragic event to you. Last night, your father died. His aging heart was unable to cope with the constant agitation any more, and he had not had a restful night's sleep for weeks.
What a cruel twist of fate, just before his dearest wish came true and you were about to come before him as a travelling merchant.
At least your father will have a burial fitting to his position. The news of his death is spreading through the town like wildfire and the citizens of {%t:01} are remembering the good deeds that he performed for the town. And anyone who was not alive to witness the way {%t:01} visibly blossomed while he was mayor is now being regaled with the story at every street corner.
Once again, your family's name is on everybody's lips, unlike before, when your father was only remembered by very few people who had relied on his support for their own careers. I wouldn't be surprised if some of this attention is to your advantage as well.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Det er min soergelige pligt at meddele jer en tragisk begivenhed. I nat doede jeres far. Hans aldrende hjerte kunne ikke laengere klare den stadige uro, og han havde ikke faaet en rolig nats soevn i ugevis.
Hvilket grusomt skaebnens lune, lige foer hans kaereste oenske skulle gaa i opfyldelse, og I skulle traede frem for ham som rejsende koebmand.
I det mindste faar jeres far en begravelse, der soemmer sig for hans stilling. Nyheden om hans doed spreder sig som en loebeild gennem byen, og borgerne i {%t:01} mindes de gode gerninger, han gjorde for byen. Og den, der ikke selv saa, hvordan {%t:01} synligt blomstrede, mens han var borgmester, faar nu historien fortalt paa hvert gadehjoerne.
Igen er jeres slaegts navn paa alles laeber, i modsaetning til foer, da jeres far kun blev husket af de faa, der havde stolet paa hans stoette i deres egne loebebaner. Det ville ikke undre mig, om noget af denne opmaerksomhed ogsaa kommer jer til gode.

Jeres ydmygeste tjener,

Karl

column2:
Young Sir,

My heartfelt congratulations on your rapid advancement. Your father's affairs are progressing normally. After the deeply moving funeral, attended by the whole of {%t:01}, the notaries, court ushers and other officials are now moving in to deal with your father's estate. I shall keep you informed about any developments.

However, I would like to tell you what I know about your father's secret, which he has now taken with him to the grave. I do not think that he would object, now that you are a recognised long distance merchant.
Unfortunately, all I can tell you is that it must have had something to do with a 'Flying Trader', as your father always mumbled about that in his sleep. When I used to take a glass of wine to him in his study late at night, he was sometimes already asleep on the couch, tossing and turning anxiously. It was on one of those occasions that I caught this name.
His nightmares must have originated from an experience that he had at sea during his youth. Your father kept in touch with one of his colleagues from that time for many years. I may be able to find out where he lives. I will write to you again once I have more news.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Mine hjerteligste lykoenskninger med jeres hurtige forfremmelse. Jeres fars anliggender skrider normalt frem. Efter den dybt bevaegende begravelse, som hele {%t:01} overvaerede, rykker notarer, retsbetjente og andre embedsmaend nu ind for at ordne jeres fars bo. Jeg holder jer underrettet om alt, der sker.

Jeg vil dog gerne fortaelle, hvad jeg ved om jeres fars hemmelighed, som han nu har taget med sig i graven. Jeg tror ikke, han ville have noget imod det, nu hvor I er en anerkendt fjernhandelsmand.
Desvaerre kan jeg kun sige, at det maa have haft noget at goere med en "Flyvende handelsmand", for det mumlede jeres far altid om i soevne. Naar jeg sent om aftenen bragte ham et glas vin i hans arbejdsvaerelse, sov han af og til allerede paa sofaen og kastede sig uroligt frem og tilbage. Ved en saadan lejlighed opfangede jeg dette navn.
Hans mareridt maa stamme fra noget, han oplevede paa havet i sin ungdom. Jeres far holdt i mange aar forbindelsen med en af sine kammerater fra dengang. Maaske kan jeg finde ud af, hvor han bor. Jeg skriver igen, saa snart jeg ved mere.

Jeres ydmygeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Sympathy
column3: Deltagelse

column2:
My dear Leopold!

You have probably never heard of me, but I was a good friend of your father's and have been following your career closely. Please accept my condolences on dear old Georg's sudden and unexpected death. If you are ever in trouble, you can turn to me with complete confidence.

Best wishes from the free town of {%t:04},
Patrician H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Min kaere Leopold!

I har sandsynligvis aldrig hoert om mig, men jeg var en god ven af jeres far og har fulgt jeres loebebane noeje. Modtag min kondolence med kaere gamle Georgs pludselige og uventede doed. Skulle I nogensinde komme i knibe, kan I med fuld tillid henvende jer til mig.

De bedste hilsner fra den frie by {%t:04},
Patricier H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: The Helmsman
column3: Styrmanden

column2:
Young Sir,

I looked in your father's personal records to try and find an address for that friend that I wrote to you about. They weren't easy documents to get hold of, as the authorities are examining all of his possessions closely. But I found out something about that old colleague of his:
Jakob Blank was the helmsman of your father's Snaikka for many years and later became his associate. He then became a councillor in {%t:05}, where he presumably still lives. He used to be a regular visitor to Luebeck, but hasn't been here in the past few years. But here is the best tip that I could find. Look for a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}, he is also known as The Helmsman!

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Jeg har ledt i jeres fars personlige papirer efter en adresse paa den ven, jeg skrev om. Det var ikke lette dokumenter at faa fat i, da myndighederne noeje gennemgaar alle hans ejendele. Men jeg fandt ud af noget om denne gamle kammerat:
Jakob Blank var i mange aar styrmand paa jeres fars snekke og blev siden hans kompagnon. Derefter blev han raadmand i {%t:05}, hvor han formentlig stadig bor. Han plejede at komme ofte til Luebeck, men har ikke vaeret her de seneste aar. Her er i hvert fald det bedste spor, jeg kunne finde. Soeg efter en vis Jakob Blank i {%t:05}, ogsaa kendt som Styrmanden!

Jeres ydmygeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Confidential Information
column3: Fortrolige oplysninger

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

You enquired about a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}. Let me give you some advice: forget that name and go back to {%t:01}.
I suspect, however, that you will not be prepared to take this advice, so I shall give you the official statement. The Jakob Blank matter has been declared confidential information at the command of a Hanseatic League session. Nobody will give you any information about this blackest period in the town's history.
The only way would be for another Hansa town to issue an official query to {%t:05}. But you would need to aquire the rank of councillor to put forward this query. And even then you would have to earn a certain reputation in {%t:05} before I could deal with your query. These strict guidelines are purely a precautionary measure and have been approved by the Hanseatic League session. Once you have fulfilled these conditions, I will tell you what you want to know.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

I har spurgt efter en vis Jakob Blank i {%t:05}. Lad mig give jer et raad: glem det navn og vend tilbage til {%t:01}.
Jeg formoder dog, at I ikke vil vaere villig til at foelge dette raad, saa jeg giver jer den officielle meddelelse. Sagen Jakob Blank er paa befaling af en hansedag erklaeret fortrolig. Ingen vil give jer oplysninger om denne sorteste periode i byens historie.
Den eneste vej ville vaere, at en anden hansestad retter en officiel forespoergsel til {%t:05}. Men I skulle have raadmands rang for at fremsaette denne forespoergsel. Og selv da maatte I opnaa en vis anseelse i {%t:05}, foer jeg kunne behandle jeres forespoergsel. Disse strenge retningslinjer er blot en forsigtighedsregel og er godkendt af hansedagen. Naar I har opfyldt disse betingelser, vil jeg fortaelle, hvad I oensker at vide.

Underskrevet: Borgmesteren
{%+:05}

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

You have enquired about a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}. Let me give you some good advice: forget that name and go back to {%t:01}.
I suspect, however, that you will not be prepared to take this advice, so I shall give you the official statement. The Jakob Blank matter has been declared confidential information at the command of a Hanseatic League session. Nobody will give you any information about this blackest period in the town's history.
The only way would be for another Hansa town to issue an official query to {%t:05}. As you occupy the rank of {%R:00}, you need only obtain a certain reputation in Riga before I can deal with your query. These strict guidelines are purely a precautionary measure and have been approved by the Hanseatic League session.
Once you have fulfilled these conditions, I will tell you what you want to know.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

I har spurgt efter en vis Jakob Blank i {%t:05}. Lad mig give jer et godt raad: glem det navn og vend tilbage til {%t:01}.
Jeg formoder dog, at I ikke vil vaere villig til at foelge dette raad, saa jeg giver jer den officielle meddelelse. Sagen Jakob Blank er paa befaling af en hansedag erklaeret fortrolig. Ingen vil give jer oplysninger om denne sorteste periode i byens historie.
Den eneste vej ville vaere, at en anden hansestad retter en officiel forespoergsel til {%t:05}. Da I baerer rang af {%R:00}, mangler I blot en vis anseelse i Riga, foer jeg kan behandle jeres forespoergsel. Disse strenge retningslinjer er blot en forsigtighedsregel og er godkendt af hansedagen.
Naar I har opfyldt disse betingelser, vil jeg fortaelle, hvad I oensker at vide.

Underskrevet: Borgmesteren
{%+:05}

column2:
With regard to the inquiry put forward by Leopold Jantzen of {%t:0B}, concerning the matter of the exiled Jakob Blank

The following information is issued:

The person Jakob Blank was banished from {%t:05} for life over 15 years ago, for jeopardising the safety of the town and 20 further offences.
At the command of a Hanseatic League session, all Hansa towns were requested to comply with this exile.
The person's last known whereabouts is {%t:07}.
This information is confidential and for official use only.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Angaaende den forespoergsel, som Leopold Jantzen fra {%t:0B} har fremsat i sagen om den forviste Jakob Blank

Foelgende oplysning gives:

Personen Jakob Blank blev for mere end 15 aar siden forvist fra {%t:05} paa livstid for at have bragt byens sikkerhed i fare og for 20 yderligere forseelser.
Paa befaling af en hansedag blev alle hansestaeder anmodet om at efterleve denne forvisning.
Personens sidst kendte opholdssted er {%t:07}.
Denne oplysning er fortrolig og kun til tjenestebrug.

Underskrevet: Borgmesteren
{%+:05}

column2: Good Advice
column3: Godt raad

column2:
Dear friend,

You are sticking your nose into things that you'd be better off steering clear of.
Please take this as good advice from one friend to another. 

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Kaere ven,

I stikker naesen i ting, som I gjorde klogest i at holde jer langt fra.
Tag det venligst som et godt raad fra ven til ven.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Dubious assistance
column3: Tvivlsom hjaelp

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

I watched you questioning people in the market square and the dark alleys of {%t:07}. It attracted my attention, as such behaviour is unusual for a man of your position.
Rumour has it that you are looking for Jakob Blank. The poor fellow was well and truly taken for a ride by your 'fine' society and put himself in our protection, so that he could disappear unnoticed. I beg your pardon - I forgot to introduce myself. You don't need to know my name - all you need to know is that I run the local guild for those who aren't so well off. I am sure you see what I mean, as I don't exactly look like a pepper sack - no offence.
Anyway, we got Jakob Blank safely underground, and my colleagues did their job so well that even I couldn't tell you where he is any more. But if he had died, I would certainly have heard about it.
As you seem to be a friend of his, I am willing to assist you in your investigations. But you must prove yourself to be trustworthy in our community first, otherwise I won't be able to achieve anything for you at all. Only when your name is known in the right circles will you find that the information you want practically seeks you out.

Farewell,
\f5_X
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

Jeg saa jer udspoerge folk paa torvet og i de moerke gyder i {%t:07}. Det vakte min opmaerksomhed, da en saadan opfoersel er usaedvanlig for en mand i jeres stilling.
Rygtet siger, at I leder efter Jakob Blank. Den stakkels fyr blev grundigt narret af jeres "fine" selskab og stillede sig under vores beskyttelse, saa han kunne forsvinde ubemaerket. Undskyld - jeg glemte at praesentere mig. Mit navn behoever I ikke kende - I behoever blot at vide, at jeg leder det stedlige lav for dem, der ikke er saa godt stillet. I forstaar sikkert, hvad jeg mener, for jeg ligner ikke ligefrem en rig koebmand - ikke ilde ment.
I hvert fald fik vi Jakob Blank i sikkerhed under jorden, og mine kolleger gjorde deres arbejde saa godt, at ikke engang jeg kan sige, hvor han er laengere. Men var han doed, havde jeg helt sikkert hoert om det.
Da I synes at vaere hans ven, er jeg villig til at hjaelpe jer i jeres eftersoegning. Men foerst maa I vise jer paalidelig i vores faellesskab, ellers kan jeg slet intet udrette for jer. Foerst naar jeres navn er kendt i de rette kredse, vil I opleve, at de oplysninger, I oensker, naermest selv opsoeger jer.

Farvel,
\f5_X

column2: Hideout
column3: Skjulested

column2: The person you are looking for is in {%t:09}.\n\n\\f5_X
column3: Den, I leder efter, befinder sig i {%t:09}.\n\n\\f5_X

column2:
My dear Leopold Jantzen,

I tried so hard to leave my wretched past behind me. But when I heard of your father's death, I knew that you would come looking for me and that my old guilt had caught up with me again.
You have doubtless come to ask me about the "Flying Trader". I will tell you what I know, but first you must do something for me.
Take me to {%t:01}, to my old friend's grave, so that I can pray for his immortal soul and also my own!
When one of your ships is in the harbour, I shall board it.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kaere Leopold Jantzen,

Jeg proevede saa haardt at laegge min elendige fortid bag mig. Men da jeg hoerte om jeres fars doed, vidste jeg, at I ville komme og lede efter mig, og at min gamle skyld igen havde indhentet mig.
I er utvivlsomt kommet for at spoerge mig om "Den flyvende handelsmand". Jeg vil fortaelle, hvad jeg ved, men foerst maa I goere noget for mig.
Foer mig til {%t:01}, til min gamle vens grav, saa jeg kan bede for hans udoedelige sjael og ogsaa for min egen!
Naar et af jeres skibe ligger i havnen, gaar jeg om bord.

Jakob Blank

column2: Estate
column3: Arv

column2:
Announcement of the decision in the matter of the estate of the {%t:01} citizen and patrician, Georg Jantzen

On the basis of an old document stored in the {%t:04} and {%t:01} archives, the authorities of the aforementioned towns agree conjointly to the following order:

As specified in writing at that time, the fortune of the Jantzen family of {%t:01} passes to the patrician Vanderdeeken of {%t:04}. The aforementioned fortune comprises not only cash but also movable and immovable items such as ships and buildings.

The fortune to be transferred also includes the aforementioned assets of {%R:00} Leopold Jantzen, where such assets can be concluded to derive from his father's wealth.
This decision is intended for immediate implementation.

{%+:01}
column3:
Bekendtgoerelse af afgoerelsen i arvesagen efter borgeren og patricieren fra {%t:01} Georg Jantzen

Paa grundlag af et gammelt dokument, der opbevares i arkiverne i {%t:04} og {%t:01}, enes myndighederne i naevnte byer i faellesskab om foelgende bestemmelse:

Som engang skriftligt fastsat overgaar familien Jantzens formue i {%t:01} til patricieren Vanderdeeken fra {%t:04}. Naevnte formue omfatter ikke blot kontanter, men ogsaa loesoere og fast ejendom saasom skibe og bygninger.

Den formue, der skal overdrages, omfatter desuden den naevnte ejendom tilhoerende {%R:00} Leopold Jantzen, for saa vidt det kan antages, at den stammer fra hans faders rigdom.
Denne afgoerelse har oejeblikkelig virkning.

{%+:01}

column2:
Poor Leopold!

You must be surprised by the recent turn of events and upset about your sudden poverty. But what were you to know what good old Georg was willing to agree to, just to make it.
I said in my letter that your father and I were old friends, and although he was always condescending towards me, I now feel almost a little sympathetic about your situation - cheated by your own father, even of what you built up yourself.
Since I'm in a lenient mood, I'd like to leave you a bit of the fortune that now rightfully belongs to me. I really don't need a second trading office in {%t:01} and I have ships and cash positively coming out of my ears.
There is no need for you to thank me for my generosity - just stay out of my way in future.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Stakkels Leopold!

I maa vaere overrasket over den seneste udvikling og bedroevet over jeres pludselige fattigdom. Men hvordan skulle I kunne vide, hvad gamle Georg var parat til for at faa succes?
Jeg skrev jo til jer, at jeres far og jeg var gamle venner, og selvom han altid var nedladende over for mig, foeler jeg nu naesten lidt medlidenhed med jeres situation: snydt af jeres egen far, endda for det, I selv har bygget op.
Da jeg er i et mildt lune, vil jeg lade jer beholde en smule af den formue, der nu med rette tilhoerer mig. Jeg har virkelig ikke brug for endnu et kontor i {%t:01}, og skibe og penge har jeg mere end nok af.
I behoever ikke takke mig for min gavmildhed; hold jer blot af vejen for mig i fremtiden.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Journey home
column3: Hjemrejse

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

I prayed at your father's grave for both of our souls. I now feel strong enough to tell you about the "Flying Trader", although not here in {%t:01}.
The curse that afflicted your father is still working even after his death and affects the whole family - I'm lucky never to have married.
So take me back to {%t:09}, please! Once we are in my own home, I will be happy to satisfy your curiosity.
When one of your ships is in the harbour, I shall board it.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg har bedt ved jeres faders grav for vore to sjaele. Nu foeler jeg mig staerk nok til at fortaelle jer om "Den flyvende koebmand", men ikke her i {%t:01}.
Den forbandelse, der hvilede over jeres far, virker endnu efter hans doed og rammer hele familien; jeg var heldig aldrig at blive gift.
Foer mig derfor tilbage til {%t:09}, vaer saa venlig! Naar jeg er hjemme i mit hus, vil jeg gerne stille jeres nysgerrighed.
Naar et af jeres skibe ligger i havnen, gaar jeg om bord.

Jakob Blank

column2: Devil's Ship
column3: Djaevleskib

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

Thank you for bringing me home safely! Now, as promised, I shall tell you about the voyage when your father and I encountered the "Flying Trader".
I presume you have already heard the story of the "Flying Trader"? - Well, the "Flying Trader" is a ghost ship that drifts around the North Sea and the Baltic. Its captain was a greedy trader who even traded with the Devil to increase his fortune. And he had certainly amassed an inconceivable fortune, which he guarded jealously aboard his vast ship.
But one day, the Devil demanded his share back, and the greedy trader refused to pay.
The Devil laughed at him and said that he would get his dues somehow. He condemned the trader to stay on his gold-laden ship and never to leave it, and never to rest until the end of time. Since then, the "Flying Trader" and his ghost ship have sailed across the northern seas, bringing misfortune on any sailors that come across the ship.
That's enough for today. You can see that telling the story has made my hands tremble. Let me rest for a day, and then I will continue with the story.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kaere unge Jantzen!

Tak fordi I bragte mig sikkert hjem! Nu vil jeg som lovet fortaelle om rejsen, hvor jeres far og jeg moedte "Den flyvende koebmand".
I har vel allerede hoert sagnet om "Den flyvende koebmand"? Nuvel, "Den flyvende koebmand" er et spoegelsesskib, der driver rundt i Nordsoeen og Oestersoeen. Dets kaptajn var en graadig koebmand, som endda handlede med djaevelen for at oege sin formue. Og han samlede sandelig en ufattelig rigdom, som han skinsygt vogtede om bord paa sit vaeldige skib.
Men en dag kraevede djaevelen sin andel, og den graadige koebmand naegtede at betale.
Djaevelen lo ad ham og sagde, at han paa den ene eller anden maade nok skulle faa sit. Han doemte koebmanden til at blive paa sit guldlastede skib uden nogensinde at forlade det, og aldrig at finde hvile til tidernes ende. Siden da sejler "Den flyvende koebmand" og hans spoegelsesskib paa de nordlige have og bringer ulykke over enhver soemand, der krydser hans vej.
Nok for i dag. I kan se, at fortaellingen har faaet mine haender til at ryste. Lad mig hvile en dag, saa fortsaetter jeg historien.

Jakob Blank

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

I promised to tell you the second part of the tale today, and I am a man of my word.
In those days your father was a young trader, just as you are now. He didn't have much and was the captain of his own Snaikka, the 'Dawn Greeting', where I was his helmsman.
We were transporting goods from {%t:04} when a sail appeared on the horizon, coming towards us. We immediately realised what was approaching us, as the 'Dawn Greeting' had just run into a pocket of calm. It could only be a ghost ship flying through the waves under full sail. Everyone knew the story of the "Flying Trader" in those days, and when the ghost ship's boat rowed over to us, we both hid behind some barrels.
A ghostly figure boarded the ship and shouted for the ship's captain, but your father and I leapt into a boat and rowed away as fast as we could.
In the next harbour we came to, we asked after the 'Dawn Greeting', but nobody had seen her anywhere. There wasn't any news over the next few weeks either, so we assumed that she had sunk in the storm and cashed in the insurance policy.
But your father and I had abandoned her, although we were the most experienced sailors on board. We could never get that guilt out of our minds.
I can just see your face now - you're taking all this with a pinch of salt and will only believe what you see with your own eyes.
I could give you a map that shows where the "Flying Trader" is, but I don't want any more dead sailors on my conscience.
You must gather a robust fleet. If you have a ship that can be used as a warship (lead ship) as well, I will show you where to look. If you use a fleet like this to sail to your ruin, none of the blame can fall on me.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg lovede at fortaelle jer anden del af historien i dag, og jeg er en mand, der holder sit ord.
Dengang var jeres far en ung handelsmand, ligesom I er nu. Han ejede ikke meget og var kaptajn paa sin egen snigge, "Morgenhilsenen", hvor jeg var hans styrmand.
Vi fragtede varer fra {%t:04}, da et sejl dukkede op i horisonten og styrede mod os. Vi forstod straks, hvad der naermede sig, for "Morgenhilsenen" var lige kommet ind i et omraade med vindstille. Det kunne kun vaere et spoegelsesskib, der floej over boelgerne for fulde sejl. Alle kendte dengang sagnet om "Den flyvende koebmand", og da spoegelsesskibets jolle roede hen mod os, gemte vi os begge bag nogle toender.
En spoegelsesagtig skikkelse kom om bord og raabte efter kaptajnen, men jeres far og jeg sprang i en jolle og roede vaek, saa hurtigt vi kunne.
I den naeste havn spurgte vi efter "Morgenhilsenen", men ingen havde set den nogen steder. Heller ikke i de foelgende uger kom der nyt, saa vi antog, at den var sunket i stormen, og haevede forsikringen.
Men jeres far og jeg havde forladt den, skoent vi var de mest erfarne soemaend om bord. Den skyld slap vi aldrig af med.
Jeg kan allerede se jeres ansigt: I tager alt dette med et gran salt og tror kun paa det, I ser med egne oejne.
Jeg kunne give jer et kort, der viser, hvor "Den flyvende koebmand" findes, men jeg vil ikke have flere doede soemaend paa samvittigheden.
I maa samle en staerk flaade. Har I desuden et skib, der kan tjene som orlogsskib (flagskib), vil jeg vise jer, hvor I skal lede. Sejler I med en saadan flaade mod jeres undergang, kan ingen skyld falde paa mig.

Jakob Blank

column2:
What a fool I am - that's what comes of tempting fate. Everyone knows that if you escape the "Flying Trader", you mustn't tell anyone about it. And I, ever the sceptic, even offered to show you where to find it.
Ever since I blabbed to you like an idiot, the previously rich town of {%t:09} has been plagued by pestilence and failed crops. Pirates are waylaying any ships that try to provide the town with even the barest essentials.
I have wrought havoc on the only place in the world that still means anything to me. {%t:09} used to have more than 3,500 inhabitants and soon it won't even be marked on the map.
Future generations will recall: {%t:09}, that was that ruined town, destroyed by one person's foolishness. Oh, misery! I can't tell you where to find the "Flying Trader". I would just bring about even greater misfortune.
Go away, and don't come back until my homeland is safe!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Hvilken taabe jeg er: saadan gaar det, naar man udfordrer skaebnen. Alle ved, at den, der undslipper "Den flyvende koebmand", ikke maa fortaelle nogen om det. Og jeg, evig skeptiker, tilboed endda at vise jer, hvor den findes.
Siden jeg plaprede som en idiot, er den engang saa rige by {%t:09} plaget af pest og misvaekst. Pirater overfalder hvert skib, der proever at bringe byen blot det allermest noedvendige.
Jeg har saaet fordaerv paa det eneste sted i verden, der endnu betyder noget for mig. {%t:09} havde over 3.500 indbyggere og vil snart ikke engang staa paa kortet.
Kommende slaegter vil huske: {%t:09}, den ruinerede by, oedelagt af en enkelt mands taabelighed. Ak og ve! Jeg kan ikke sige jer, hvor "Den flyvende koebmand" findes. Det ville kun bringe endnu stoerre ulykke.
Gaa, og kom ikke tilbage, foer mit hjemland er reddet!

Jakob Blank

column2: Sorry figure
column3: Soergelig skikkelse

column2:
Brave Leopold!

Have you taken it upon yourself to save this godforsaken town? The citizens of {%t:09} certainly don't deserve it for harbouring that wretched sinner Blank. He was driven out of {%t:05} in disgrace, but what a joke that turned out to be. {%t:09} just flung open its gates to him because he made a generous donation to the town's coffers. That went straight into the fat councillors' pockets.
{%t:09}'s prosperous years are in the past, and believe me, even you can't bring them back!

H. Vanderdeeken
column3:
Tapre Leopold!

Har I sat jer for at redde denne gudsforladte by? Borgerne i {%t:09} fortjener det sandelig ikke, fordi de tog imod den usle synder Blank. Han blev jaget ud af {%t:05} i vanaere, men sikke en komedie det blev. {%t:09} slog portene paa vid gab for ham, fordi han gav en gavmild gave til bykassen. Som gik direkte i lommerne paa de fede raadsherrer.
{%t:09}s gode aar er forbi, og tro mig, ikke engang I kan bringe dem tilbage!

H. Vanderdeeken

column2:
Noble Jantzen!

Saviour of {%t:09}, you have shown true courage by protecting my home from the raging storms of destiny. Your success has strengthened my resolve to entrust you with my last secret: the position where the "Flying Trader" is most likely to be found. Once you have a ship that can be used as a warship, and that is therefore suitable for this delicate mission, I will give you the location at last.

Take care, and may God be with you!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Aedle Jantzen!

Redningsmand for {%t:09}, I har vist aegte mod ved at beskytte mit hjemland mod skaebnens rasende storme. Jeres succes har styrket min beslutning om at betro jer min sidste hemmelighed: stedet, hvor "Den flyvende koebmand" mest sandsynligt findes. Saa snart I har et skib, der kan tjene som orlogsskib og dermed egner sig til denne delikate mission, vil jeg endelig give jer stedet.

Vaer forsigtig, og Gud vaere med jer!

Jakob Blank

column2: Musty Old Hulk
column3: Gammel muggen holk

column2:
Honourable Sir,

We made our way to the position marked on the map and waited there. Suddenly the wind subsided and we drifted slowly with the current. There was a second ship with tattered sails floating across towards our course in a strong current. When a slight breeze started again, we boarded the ship and searched it from top to bottom.
It was nothing more than a derelict hulk, with stacks of empty, rotten chests and cases in its hold.
There was no crew on board, nor any other signs that it had been used recently. We sank the ship in the ocean according to your orders, and I am pleased to enclose a full report for you.

With nautical wishes,

Helmsman of the {%s:06}
column3:
Aerede herre!

Vi satte kurs mod det sted, der var afmaerket paa kortet, og ventede der. Pludselig loejede vinden af, og vi drev langsomt med stroemmen. Et andet skib med laset sejl drev ind mod vores kurs i en staerk stroem. Da en let brise atter blaeste op, entrede vi skibet og gennemsoegte det fra top til bund.
Det var intet andet end en forladt holk med bunker af tomme, raadne kister og kasser i lastrummet.
Der var ingen besaetning om bord og heller intet andet tegn paa, at den var blevet brugt for nylig. Vi saenkede skibet i havet efter jeres ordre, og jeg har den fornoejelse at vedlaegge en fuldstaendig rapport.

Med soemandshilsen,

Styrmanden paa {%s:06}

column2:
Brave Jantzen!

I have heard about your encounter with the ghost ship. As you and your entire crew have escaped with your lives, it would seem that the curse of the "Flying Trader" has finally been broken. Seafaring is therefore greatly indebted to you, but I am even more indebted to you, for you have lifted a dark shadow from my soul. There is a rumour that you are now hoping to be elected mayor in Bremen, so that you can put that self-satisfied Vanderdeeken in his place. I would love to be there with you, but, now that I am free of my terrible burden, I imagine I shall soon be peacefully entering the realms of the dead.

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
Tapre Jantzen!

Jeg har hoert om jeres moede med spoegelsesskibet. Da I og hele jeres besaetning slap derfra med livet i behold, synes forbandelsen over "Den flyvende koebmand" endelig at vaere brudt. Soefarten staar altsaa i stor gaeld til jer, men jeg endnu mere, for I har fjernet en moerk skygge fra min sjael. Det siges, at I nu haaber at blive valgt til borgmester i Bremen for at saette den hovne Vanderdeeken paa plads. Hvor gerne ville jeg ikke vaere der med jer, men nu da jeg er fri for min frygtelige byrde, gaar jeg vel snart i fred ind i de doedes rige.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2: Mayor
column3: Borgmester

column2:
Young Sir,

I would like to congratulate you on your recent deeds. There has been a splendid atmosphere in the house since the latest news about you arrived.
News of your plan to become mayor of {%t:04} has already spread throughout the Hanseatic League. Even a cousin from Novgorod contacted us to wish you luck.
The inhabitants of your old home town will certainly be sorry to lose their most celebrated {%R:00}, but everybody is hoping that you will teach the unpopular Vanderdeeken a lesson by becoming mayor of his home town.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Jeg vil gerne lykoenske jer med jeres seneste bedrifter. Siden de seneste nyheder om jer kom, hersker der en straalende stemning i huset.
Nyheden om jeres plan om at blive borgmester i {%t:04} har allerede bredt sig over hele Hansaen. Selv en faetter fra Novgorod har meldt sig for at oenske jer held og lykke.
Indbyggerne i jeres gamle hjemby vil sikkert savne deres mest beroemte {%R:00}, men alle haaber, at I vil give den upopulaere Vanderdeeken en laerestreg ved at blive borgmester i hans egen by.

Jeres tro tjener,

Karl

column2: Legacy
column3: Testamente

column2:
Now then, young Jantzen!

So you think you can offer me your services in Bremen? Or maybe not - I hear that you want to become mayor of my town. And the rabble and fat cats are encouraging you in this recklessness.
Let me give you this warning: the people that are so fond of you at the moment are driven by envy. They envy my wealth and power, but they secretly admire and fear me.
They would never utter a single word against me and I'll give you some honest advice - do the same thing.
Well, you may be able to sink rotten ships, but in my view you're nothing more than a ne'er-do-well, brought up by his father to have too high an opinion of himself.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Naa, unge Jantzen!

Saa I tror, I kan tilbyde mig jeres tjenester i Bremen? Eller maaske ikke: jeg hoerer, at I vil vaere borgmester i min by. Og poebelen og de store kanoner opmuntrer jer i dette overmod.
Lad mig advare jer: de folk, der nu holder saa meget af jer, drives af misundelse. De misunder mig min rigdom og min magt, men i hemmelighed beundrer og frygter de mig.
De ville aldrig sige et ondt ord om mig, og jeg giver jer et oprigtigt raad: goer det samme.
I kan maaske saenke raadne skibe, men for mig er I intet andet end en doegenigt, som jeres far opdrog med alt for hoeje tanker om sig selv.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Honesty
column3: Aerlighed

column2:
My dear colleague, Mr Jantzen,

I am truly concerned about your soul. Your father had to pledge the full extent of his future wealth to make half as much progress, and I can't imagine what shady deals you have done to propell you upwards so quickly.
I can't believe that the sudden wealth that you are flaunting with such a lack of restraint is the result of good, honest hard work. I do hope you aren't making the same mistake your father did!

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Min kaere kollega, hr. Jantzen!

Jeg er virkelig bekymret for jeres sjael. Jeres far maatte pantsaette hele sin fremtidige formue for at naa halvvejs, og jeg toer ikke forestille mig, hvilke lyssky forretninger der har drevet jer saa hurtigt opad.
Jeg kan ikke tro, at den pludselige rigdom, I saa ugenert stiller til skue, er frugten af godt, aerligt og haardt arbejde. Jeg haaber ikke, I begaar den samme fejl som jeres far!

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
Dear Mayor Jantzen,

Some time ago, a letter postmarked {%t:09} arrived, addressed to "Mayor Jantzen of {%t:04}". We assumed that this was a mistake and returned it to the sender. But the letter came back to us, again postmarked {%t:09}, and lay forgotten until your inauguration reminded me of it again.
It seems to me that the letter must be intended for you and, now that you are mayor, I can give it to you.

{%t:04} Post office
column3:
Kaere borgmester Jantzen!

For nogen tid siden kom et brev stemplet i {%t:09}, adresseret til "borgmester Jantzen i {%t:04}". Vi troede, det var en fejl, og sendte det tilbage til afsenderen. Men brevet kom tilbage til os, igen stemplet i {%t:09}, og laa glemt hen, indtil jeres tiltraedelse mindede mig om det.
Det forekommer mig, at brevet maa vaere tiltaenkt jer, og nu da I er borgmester, kan jeg overraekke det.

Postkontoret i {%t:04}

column2: Guilt
column3: Skyld

column2:
\f1_Here is the letter that was kept for you.
\f3_

\r{%t:09}, {%D:10}
\lWhat a wretched sinner I am!

A short time ago, one of my few old friends visited me in the bed where I shall soon be meeting my maker. He was to tell me every detail that he knew of the events surrounding your voyage to the ghost ship. It was with horror that I learnt from his account that you did not actually make the voyage yourself.
Of course, this changes everything. As you had your father's money in your pocket, you should have seen the ghost ship. Once again, I have brought twice, three times as much guilt upon myself and am writing this letter so that I can warn you at least of the impending doom.

Didn't you mention last time we met that you were now mayor of {%t:04}? If that is the case, this letter will doubtless have reached you promptly, and at least you will be able to save your soul. But one thing at a time:
I didn't tell you the whole truth about the "Flying Trader" and my encounter with the ghost ship.

Anyone who encounters the ghost ship with a pure conscience and without desire for profit will see nothing more than a ship that has been weathered over the centuries, and is in absolutely no danger.
But anyone on board with greed in his heart or who carries any of the ghost ship's treasure in his purse will be greeted by the apparition of the miserly trader, who will propose a deal. Those who accept will receive a share of the trader's treasure and will sell the souls of any respectable sailors aboard the ship in return.
The treasure is bewitched and multiplies as if by itself, but it is cursed to find its way back to its master and ultimately to bring the unlawful owner nothing but misfortune.

In those days, your father's business was not going very well and he had fallen for a beautiful lady in Luebeck, whose father wanted nothing to do with a poor son-in-law. I had gambled away a lot of money, and so before that fateful voyage, we found ourselves sitting in an inn in Bremen discussing our problems, when a stranger approached our table. He knew all about our difficulties and offered to help us. All he wanted in return was a fair share of our future wealth. We agreed, having nothing to lose, and he told us that on our next voyage we would happen upon a ship with which we could conduct the transaction of our lives.
I don't need to tell you the details of what happened next, as you have surely guessed them already. We sold the 'Dawn Greeting' to the "Flying Trader" and made it to dry land with a rowing boat full of gold.
From then on, fortune seemed to smile upon us. Your father got his girl and forged a fabulous career for himself in {%t:01}. I paid my debts and won plenty more money besides, until one day the stranger appeared again. First of all, he demanded that your father give him his sweet little daughter. Then he came to me: I refused to give in to his demands and was chased from what was then my home, labelled a common criminal. Since then, I went on the run time and time again and lost touch with your father. It was only in {%t:09} that I found my way back to a reasonably normal life, although I never touched the money that I had left. And now I shall have to go to my grave with new sins because I failed to tell you the whole truth in time. All I can do now is advise you to hide all of your father's money and all that I am leaving you for safe keeping. Do not touch it, and under no circumstances must you use it in an attempt to increase it, otherwise the curse of the "Flying Trader" will find you and you will know no more peace in this world!

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
\f1_Her er brevet, der er blevet opbevaret til jer.
\f3_

\r{%t:09}, {%D:10}
\lHvilken elendig synder jeg er!

For nylig besoegte en af mine faa gamle venner mig ved det leje, hvor jeg snart skal moede min Skaber. Han skulle fortaelle mig hver eneste detalje, han kendte, om jeres rejse til spoegelsesskibet. Med raedsel erfarede jeg af hans beretning, at I ikke selv foretog rejsen.
Det aendrer naturligvis alt. Da I bar jeres faders penge i lommen, burde I have set spoegelsesskibet. Endnu en gang har jeg paadraget mig dobbelt, tredobbelt skyld, og jeg skriver dette brev for i det mindste at advare jer mod det truende fordaerv.

Naevnte I ikke ved vort sidste moede, at I nu er borgmester i {%t:04}? Er det tilfaeldet, har dette brev sikkert naaet jer hurtigt, og I kan i det mindste redde jeres sjael. Men lad mig tage det fra begyndelsen:
Jeg fortalte ikke hele sandheden om "Den flyvende koebmand" og mit moede med spoegelsesskibet.

Den, der moeder spoegelsesskibet med ren samvittighed og uden vindesyge, ser intet andet end et skib maerket af aarhundreder og er ikke i nogen fare.
Men den, der er om bord med graadighed i hjertet eller baerer noget af spoegelsesskibets skat i sin pung, bliver moedt af den gerrige koebmands genfaerd, som foreslaar en handel. De, der tager imod den, faar en del af koebmandens skat og saelger til gengaeld sjaelene hos alle haederlige soemaend om bord.
Skatten er forhekset og formerer sig ligesom af sig selv, men den er forbandet: den finder tilbage til sin herre og bringer til sidst den uretmaessige ejer intet andet end ulykke.

Dengang gik jeres faders forretninger ikke saerlig godt, og han havde forelsket sig i en smuk dame fra Luebeck, hvis far ikke ville vide af en fattig svigersoen. Jeg havde tabt mange penge paa spil, og saa sad vi foer den skaebnesvangre rejse paa en kro i Bremen og talte om vore sorger, da en fremmed kom hen til vores bord. Han vidste alt om vore vanskeligheder og tilboed at hjaelpe os. Alt, hvad han ville have til gengaeld, var en rimelig andel af vor fremtidige rigdom. Vi sagde ja, for vi havde intet at miste, og han sagde, at vi paa vor naeste rejse ville stoede paa et skib, med hvilket vi ville goere vort livs handel.
Jeg behoever ikke fortaelle, hvad der skete siden, det har I sikkert allerede gaettet. Vi solgte "Morgenhilsenen" til "Den flyvende koebmand" og naaede fast land i en robaad fuld af guld.
Siden da syntes lykken at smile til os. Jeres far fik sin pige og gjorde en eventyrlig karriere i {%t:01}. Jeg betalte min gaeld og vandt desuden mange penge, indtil den fremmede en dag dukkede op igen. Foerst forlangte han, at jeres far skulle give ham sin soede lille datter. Saa kom han til mig: jeg naegtede at boeje mig for hans krav og blev jaget ud af det, der dengang var mit hjem, stemplet som en simpel forbryder. Siden da er jeg flygtet igen og igen og har mistet forbindelsen med jeres far. Foerst i {%t:09} vendte jeg tilbage til et nogenlunde normalt liv, skoent jeg aldrig roerte de penge, jeg havde tilbage. Og nu maa jeg gaa i graven med nye synder, fordi jeg ikke fortalte jer hele sandheden i tide. Alt, hvad jeg kan goere nu, er at raade jer til at gemme alle jeres faders penge og alt, hvad jeg efterlader jer, i forvaring. Roer det ikke, og brug det under ingen omstaendigheder til at forsoege at formere det, ellers vil forbandelsen over "Den flyvende koebmand" finde jer, og I vil ikke kende ro mere i denne verden!

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2:
Accursed Jantzen!

Why do you always have to meddle in things you don't understand?
You evidently have a certain talent for manipulating people, Mr Mayor of {%t:04}.
That's how you've managed to become my superior here in my home town of {%t:04}, not that that matters, as I still have countless other titles!
You can gloat and rejoice as much as you like, but I'll get what's mine in the end. Sooner or later we will meet again - and that's a promise.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Forbandede Jantzen!

Hvorfor skal I altid blande jer i ting, I ikke forstaar?
I har aabenbart et vist talent for at manipulere folk, hr. borgmester i {%t:04}.
Saadan er I blevet min overordnede her i min hjemby {%t:04}, ikke at det betyder noget, for jeg har endnu utallige andre titler!
I maa fryde jer og glaede jer, saa meget I vil, men til sidst faar jeg det, der er mit. Foer eller siden moedes vi igen, det lover jeg.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

The legend of the Kobold is circulating amongst the crew again. I have heard of instances where the crew have got so worked up that they have put the whole ship in danger.
I shall be harder on the sailors than usual, so that they can get this dangerous superstition out of their heads as quickly as possible.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Sagnet om skibsnissen gaar igen rundt blandt besaetningen. Jeg har hoert om tilfaelde, hvor besaetninger blev saa ophidsede, at de bragte hele skibet i fare.
Jeg vil vaere haardere ved soemaendene end ellers, saa de hurtigst muligt faar denne farlige overtro ud af hovedet.

Styrmanden paa {%s:04}

column2: Anxiety
column3: Uro

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Once again, those gullible scaredicats have picked up something about the Kobold. It is this very spirit that protects every ship, and legend says that if he should ever disembark, the ship would be lost, including its crew and cargo. You will have heard the tale that the Kobold is supposed to show himself just before he leaves the ship. But now these tars reckon they're seeing the Kobold leering out at them from behind every plank.
Morale is not at its highest, so it might be better if you took care of this yourself!

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Endnu en gang har de godtroende kujoner opfanget noget om skibsnissen. Det er netop denne aand, der beskytter hvert skib, og sagnet siger, at hvis han nogensinde gaar fra borde, er skibet tabt, med besaetning og last. I har vel hoert, at skibsnissen skal vise sig lige foer han forlader skibet. Men nu mener disse soeulke at se nissen grine ad dem bag hver planke.
Moralen er ikke paa sit hoejeste, saa det var maaske bedre, hvis I selv tog jer af det!

Styrmanden paa {%s:04}

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

One of the older sailors told the younger ones that the Kobold leaves any ship whose owner acts in a way that is displeasing to God.
I have managed to calm the crew down by telling them that you were renowned for your honesty throughout the entire Hanseatic League. Now everybody on board is concentrating on their duties again.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

En af de aeldre soemaend fortalte de yngre, at skibsnissen forlader ethvert skib, hvis ejer handler paa en maade, der mishager Gud.
Jeg har faaet besaetningen beroliget ved at sige, at I er kendt i hele Hansaen for jeres aerlighed. Nu koncentrerer alle om bord sig igen om deres pligter.

Styrmanden paa {%s:04}

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

This time, even members of our own crew say they have seen the ghost ship. And now that the crew has heard talk in the {%t:07} taverns about a ship that is long overdue, there are rumours going round that it has been captured by the 'Flying Trader'.
You will not be surprised to learn that all this unfortunate speculation has damaged the crew's morale.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Denne gang siger selv folk fra vores egen besaetning, at de har set spoegelsesskibet. Og nu, hvor besaetningen har hoert snak i kroerne i {%t:07} om et skib, der laenge har vaeret forsinket, gaar der rygter om, at det er blevet kapret af "Den flyvende koebmand".
Det vil ikke overraske jer, at al denne uheldige spekulation har skadet besaetningens moral.

Styrmanden paa {%s:04}

column2:
{%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

You must help me! My only daughter was kidnapped by pirates 5 days ago. The pirate was {%N:06}, who seems an insidious specimen, who somehow managed to board our ship. Please help me while there is still hope for my daughter.
Give me your decision within 10 days.

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}
column3:
{%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

I maa hjaelpe mig! Min eneste datter blev bortfoert af pirater for 5 dage siden. Piraten var {%N:06}, en lumsk type, som paa en eller anden maade fik entret vores skib. Hjaelp mig, beder jeg, mens der endnu er haab for min datter.
Giv mig jeres beslutning inden 10 dage.

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}

column2:
Dear {%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

Thank you for agreeing to help me. The pirate was last seen 1 day's journey north of Edinburgh. If I were you, that would be the first place I'd look for him. But take care! You must not sink his ship; you must board it! He has a cog with at least 30 men who are armed to the teeth!
If my daughter isn't back here with me in {%t:03} in 30 days, I will assume that you have failed.

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}
column3:
Kaere {%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

Tak fordi I har sagt ja til at hjaelpe mig. Piraten blev sidst set 1 dagsrejse nord for Edinburgh. Var jeg jer, ville jeg lede efter ham der foerst. Men vaer forsigtig! I maa ikke saenke hans skib, I skal entre det! Han har en kogge med mindst 30 mand, bevaebnet til taenderne!
Er min datter ikke tilbage hos mig i {%t:03} inden 30 dage, gaar jeg ud fra, at I har fejlet.

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}

column2:
Dear {%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

I am so overjoyed at my daughter's safe return. Although I can barely express my gratitude with a reward, I hope you will accept these 30,000\C.
But there is something else that would give me even greater pleasure. Would you care to take my daughter to be your wife?

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}
column3:
Kaere {%R:02} {%v:02} {%n:02},

Jeg er saa lykkelig over, at min datter er kommet sikkert hjem. Selvom en beloenning knap kan udtrykke min taknemmelighed, haaber jeg, at I vil tage imod disse 30.000\C.
Men der er noget, der ville glaede mig endnu mere. Vil I tage min datter til hustru?

{%R:04} {%v:04} {%n:04}
